mathematical_discussion:
本步确立了研究对象的精确基线，并把庞大的继承理论压缩为几个彼此不可混淆的数学问题。继承稿实际采用的尺度不变 Einstein 缺陷为 E(g)=inf_{lambda≠0} ∫|Ric_g-lambda g|²/(lambda²Vol_g)，允许类应明确为固定闭光滑四维流形上的全部光滑 Riemann 度量。若 R=∫|Ric|²>0，则 E=4-(∫s)²/(Vol·R)=J+∫(s-s_bar)²/R，其中 J=4∫|Ric°|²/R；Ricci-flat 情形反而有 E=4。因此正间隙、零下确界、下确界达到和 Einstein 度量存在确实是不同层次。现有 actual-field 理论已经给出两个强而互补的正间隙机制：N1 在每个共形类有同一实际 monopole 解、p≥A 时控制 J+(T_+/A-2/3)_+；I40/I41 的 compatible-background cancellation 则把 scalar surplus 和 p-T_+ 线性压到 P+D_2，并在两手征拓扑窗口产生线性尺度。它们在 balanced surgery family 上与真实 recovery metrics 匹配，得到 c h≤alpha≤4h/(1+h)，但只确定线性阶，不确定一般 blowup/handle 平衡下的一阶系数。handle-only 子族则已有精确值 4h/(1+h) 及 0<h<1/3 时不达到。另一方面，固定 Dehn-twist surface bundle E_D 上存在同一光滑流形的度量 G_l，使 Vol 固定、sup|G_l^{-1}(Ric+G_l)|→0 且各阶曲率有统一控制，从而 E(G_l)→0，故 alpha(E_D)=0。其 injectivity radius→0、diameter→∞，显示消失间隙来自全局退化而非局部曲率失控。该流形及所有有限覆盖具有双向 actual monopoles，并排除复结构与非正截面曲率度量，却尚未排除远处的负 Einstein 度量。因 E=0 等价于某个非零 Einstein 倍数，且非负 Einstein 与 Ricci-flat 已被排除，所以这里下确界达到等价于存在负 Einstein 度量；现有构造只排除了所展示共形类中的 Einstein 修正和靠近 G_l 的连续归一化 Einstein 分支。这一固定流形把 alpha=0 与精确存在问题之间的断裂具体化，是整个理论不可忽略的退化模型。
对 balanced family，最关键的未闭合量已被精确还原为 p_j=inf∫|Ric°|²：alpha_j=4p_j/(8π²A_j)+O(h_j²)，所以系数四等价于 p_j=8π²Q_j+o(Q_j)。LeBrun 的经典结果只给 inf∫|Ric|²=8π²(A+Q) 与 inf∫s²=32π²A；两个下确界不能相减，因为所需的是同一度量上的 scalar-Weyl 补偿。继承稿已给出三种真正接触此缺口的结构。其一是符号分解 P=8π²N+Z，所需正是 Z≥8π²(Q-N)-o(Q)，而不是分别强迫 N 或 Z。其二是 simultaneous monopole identity P-8π²Q=A_field-4 average(K)，其缺失信息是 signed kinetic term 至多等于非负 remainder 加 o(Q)。其三是 whole-AE-core 拓扑代价：若 near-minimizer 的完整标记核心及端部修正能以 o(Q) 精度恢复，则每个 exceptional class 花费 8π²、每个 handle 花费 32π²；但一般 ideal-minimizer 理论尚不能从仅有 O(A) 总能量恢复这些标记与精度。
一个可能改变 O11 判断、值得优先发展而不能被现有下界思路遮蔽的方向来自 Malchiodi–Malizia 的 2025 strict Weyl connected-sum construction。固定拓扑上有同一度量恒等式 ΔP=2ΔW_op+ΔS/12，因此单独严格降低 Weyl energy 并不足够；必须计算该具体 glued conformal class 经负 Yamabe 代表替换后的 scalar cost，并与 Weyl saving 在相同 a^4 阶比较。若每个 blowup site 的净 P 变化为负，并可在 complex-hyperbolic covers 上对正比例于 Q 的稀疏互不相交 sites 统一复制，就会给出低于系数四的真实上构造；若净变化非负且可由二次形式解释，则可能反过来揭示全竞争者下界的局部机制。2026 LCF-factor 定理要求非半自对偶的 Bach-flat 因子，不能直接套到 complex-hyperbolic 半自对偶背景；2025 定理的手征条件与具体 orientation 必须从原证明核实。这个同度量联合展开，比继续分别研究 Weyl 与 scalar 下确界更可能改变核心判断。
无密度端点 O10 也是高价值问题，但其所有固定 Euler-density 版本已经证明；任何反例序列必须满足 chi/A→∞，并同时具有完整 actual conformal supply、beta→∞、kappa_beta→0。现有径向方法只剩中等 amplitude transition 与第五张量幂方程的 retained mass/full weak equation 同时闭合问题。与 balanced family 已经明确的同度量一阶代价相比，O10 当前需要更大范围的新信息，故不宜在尚未比较联合 gluing 展开前成为唯一主线。整体研究方向应同时保留：正间隙的 actual-field 兼容性原理、alpha=0 的 collapse/shear 机制、同度量最优代价、以及达到性与精确 Einstein 存在；任何统一理论都必须解释这四者为何在不同拓扑和退化方式下分离或重新耦合。

research_summary:
Starting from the Step 1 handoff (O11 joint gluing route), I read CLAIMS_AND_CORRECTIONS.md and found that the inherited corpus already contains the fixed-collar cell formulation: I54 = Skills/geometric-analysis/research/sources/continuation/20260928_relative_cell_cost.md and I55 = .../20260928_localization_and_coupled_filling.md. I read both in full where relevant: cell identities (1.1)–(1.2); finite-cell transfer (2.1)–(2.3); the Kähler cost (3.2); Theorem 1 excluding conformally Kähler cells; the triaxial almost-Kähler reduction (6.3)–(6.11); triaxial descent (6.8); the general bound J ≥ 8π^2q − 4d/3 (7.2); Prop. 2 (no smooth stationary cell); I55 Theorem 1 with fixed exterior; Prop. 5 radial moment (8.2)–(8.5), which excludes φ = 0; and Prop. 6, a two-scale requirement. Before finding these I had re-derived the cell identity myself, the 'Φ-density' ∫|Ric+g|^2 − 8π^2 = ∫(4|W^+|^2+(s+3)^2/3+1) − 4d, which matches I54 (1.2). I then derived its global form 4𝒲 + 𝒮 with 𝒮 ≥ 0 by LeBrun, together with the exact coefficient-four statement for metrics with |W^+|^2 ≥ s^2/24.

I then built a numerical framework for the open conformal triaxial class. workspace/scripts/cell_ricci.py derives the Bianchi-IX Ricci of G = e^{2φ}K with sympy; it matches I54 (6.10) term by term. workspace/scripts/cell_opt.py uses a Chebyshev log-radial parametrization with exact bolt conditions F(r0)=0, F'(r0)=2/r0, w = O((r−r0)^2) and an exact CH collar beyond Rc (C^3 matching), with torch float64 and L-BFGS. workspace/scripts/check_kahler_identity.py confirms the Kähler identity j = (2+μ)^2 + ½∫(s+4)^2r^3dr to 1e-13. Two sweeps followed. sweep1.sh (data/cell_sweep1, 224 runs) covered Rc 0.8–3, μ 0.001–0.6, biaxial-conformal and full modes. sweep2.sh / cell_stage2.py (data/cell_stage2, 15 cases at degree 24) computed autograd Hessians and 12 kicked restarts per case; plot_cells.py produced figures/cell_cost_vs_bound.png.

Results: min j − 4 = 0.0040, with j_best − 4 ≈ 4μ + μ^2. All optima sit above the bound (2+μ)^2/(1−μ^2/R^4), with min excess 2.8e-6. Examples: R = 4, μ = 0.01 gives 4.04015 against a bound of 4.04010; R = 4, μ = 0.1 gives 4.41232 against 4.41017. The smallest w-Hessian eigenvalues are about 1e-9 to 1e-7 (near-null basis directions) and the largest 60–5000. Triaxial kicks lower j by at most about 1e-2, and only in expensive cells (μ = 0.3, R = 1: 11.455 → 11.445). From these results I formulated Conjecture C1 and the conditional bubbling proof route for the cell conjecture. Everything is recorded in workspace/notes/step2_cell_problem_and_triaxial_numerics.md. I replied to peer S1003A02 (message 739, replying to 738) with the results and file paths. The numerics cover a finite-dimensional, cohomogeneity-one class and prove nothing beyond it; no new theorem has been proved this step.
continuation:
Decide the main O11 line using the new state. There are three serious, complementary directions.

(A) Prove Conjecture C1, which closes I55's (8.4) window in the whole conformal triaxial class. Use the actual quantities N, B_0 and A_0 from I54 (6.6)–(6.7a), the radial moment (8.2) and the scalar identity (8.6). The numerics suggest the triaxial anisotropy splits the repeated W^+ eigenvalue, so B_0 should dominate any formal gain from nonintegrability. A Wolfram/sympy check of a candidate inequality B_0 ≳ f(N) on actual profiles would test this cheaply.

(B) Push the construction side beyond the diagonal class. Extend cell_opt.py to non-diagonal SU(2)-invariant metrics, U(1)-invariant metrics, and a two-centre or fixed-neck Malchiodi–Malizia-type cell. Evaluate the same-metric 4𝒲 + 𝒮 identity to see whether any configuration depletes W^+ by more than a quarter of its scalar excess. An actual subthreshold cell would give coefficient < 4 on the real balanced family through I54 (2.3), and its energy should then be certified rigorously (interval arithmetic, CAPD/Arb).

(C) Develop the finite-energy lower-bound theorem: cell conjecture ⟸ compactness modulo AE bubble trees for J-minimizing cells. This means a Sacks–Uhlenbeck-type regularization J_ε = J + ε∫|Rm|^p (p > 2) or + ε∫|∇Ric|^2, ε-regularity uniform in ε, an energy identity, and exclusion of interior collapse. Retrieve the precise statements of Tian–Viaclovsky ε-regularity for critical metrics of quadratic functionals, Petersen–Wei/Anderson L^p-curvature compactness, and any minimizing-sequence results for ∫|Ric|^2-type functionals in dimension 4. Then judge whether the analytic gap is attackable now.

Keep the separate branches alive: the fixed bundle E_D (α = 0, attainment ⇔ a negative Einstein metric), and O10 together with the peer's radial-capacity proposal from S1003A02 note step1_field_compatibility_and_route_portfolio.md. Use a TTCS generator or verifier for C1 or for the bubbling reduction if it would sharpen the choice. Files: workspace/notes/step2_cell_problem_and_triaxial_numerics.md, workspace/scripts/cell_*.py, data/cell_sweep1, data/cell_stage2, figures/cell_cost_vs_bound.png.
mathematical_discussion:
The balanced optimal-coefficient question (O11) now reduces to a sharp local problem plus a separate bulk-extraction problem. This step derived an all-metric global identity. On any balanced-family member, with 2χ+3τ = A−Q and the inherited monopole supply giving (c^+)^2 ≥ A, it reads ∫|Ric+g|^2 − 8π^2Q = 4𝒲 + 𝒮, where 𝒲 = ∫|W^+|^2 − (4π^2/3)A and 𝒮 = ∫((s+3)^2/3+1) − (8π^2/3)A. The term 𝒮 is ≥ 0 for every metric, by LeBrun's ∫s^2 ≥ 32π^2(c^+)^2. So a coefficient below four can only come from depleting self-dual Weyl energy below its Kähler–Einstein value, and the scalar excess 𝒮 that the same metric pays must be less than four times that depletion. Two consequences follow. First, coefficient four holds exactly, with no error term, for every metric with |W^+|^2 ≥ s^2/24 pointwise, including every Kähler metric. Second, the two Seiberg–Witten estimates alone give only −(8π^2/3)A, with an extremal W^+ one quarter of the Kähler ratio. The missing information is therefore differential: how much W^+ an actual metric can lose and what that costs. Algebra alone cannot supply it. This is the global form of the inherited cell identity I54 (1.2), which I first re-derived independently and then found already in the corpus. The construction side thus becomes a fixed-collar cell problem. Any smooth blowup cell of a complex-hyperbolic (CH) ball with J < 8π^2 would lower the coefficient on the actual family, by I54 (2.2)–(2.3). Coefficient four therefore implies the cell conjecture J ≥ 8π^2q, and this conjecture is a finite-energy O(1) problem. That is structurally easier than the global route, where o(Q) precision has to be extracted from an O(A) energy budget.

I ran the first numerical attack on the largest class the inherited work had left open: conformal triaxial SU(2)-diagonal one-bolt cells, with F, w and φ all free. I54 Theorem 1 excludes only the conformally Kähler subclass, and I55 Prop. 5 excludes only φ = 0; the middle window (8.4) was open. The numerics give no subthreshold cell. Every optimum stays above the Theorem 1 conformally Kähler bound (2+μ)^2/(1−μ^2/R^4) and nearly touches it for large collar radius R. The triaxial direction w helps only in expensive cells and never crosses the threshold, and the w-Hessian at the conformal-biaxial optimum is positive semidefinite. This motivates Conjecture C1: Theorem 1 extends to the whole conformal almost-Kähler diagonal class, and the cell infimum in this class is the value (2+μ)^2 → 4, carried by the exceptional area and approached only as the bolt shrinks. This is consistent with I54 Prop. 2, that no smooth cell is stationary: in the symmetric class the problem does not attain its infimum.

This non-attainment suggests a conditional lower-bound proof of the cell conjecture. Take a minimizing sequence of cells and suppose it is compact modulo AE bubble trees, with no interior collapse. If the topology stays in the limit, the limit is a smooth minimizer, hence stationary, which Prop. 2 forbids. Otherwise the bubbles carry the topology and each exceptional class costs ≥ 8π^2, because an AE metric on O(−1) has P = 8π^2 + 2∫(2|W^+|^2+s^2/24). The remaining analytic theorem is a Sacks–Uhlenbeck-type regularization of the critical L^2-Ricci functional, with ε-regularity and an energy identity, plus an argument excluding collapse. The volume window 4d/9 < Vol < 4d (d the volume of the replaced ball) holds for subthreshold cells but does not by itself rule out collapse. This is a real theorem to prove and is not yet available. On construction, coefficient-changing candidates must leave the cohomogeneity-one diagonal class: non-diagonal SU(2) cells, U(1)-invariant cells, or fixed-neck Malchiodi–Malizia-type gluings oriented to make 𝒲 < 0. Each has to be tested with the same-metric 4𝒲 + 𝒮 accounting. The fixed manifold E_D (α = 0, attainment equivalent to a negative Einstein metric) and the O10 endpoint remain separate open branches, not addressed this step.

继续处于 Explore，但用有区分力的计算攻击真正剩余的 profile 机制，而不是再做无约束极小化。首先扩展 workspace/scripts/cell_compensation.py，直接约束或奖励 q=T_phi−P_w>0，并分别在固定 μ、μ→0、固定物理 transition radius 与 inner scaling r=√μ x 下搜索。目标不是单纯降低 j，而是确定能否进入 0<q<2M0 的径向危险区，同时控制 X、Y、Z、V_w 四个 residual；记录最小 j−K、q、N、每项支付、F 的正性、分辨率和重启稳定性。至少使用两种 parametrization 或 continuation：从 I55 的 M=0 共形 zero-moment profile 出发加入 w，以及从低成本 Kähler recovery 出发逐步提高 q。若出现 C1 负值，必须提高 degree/quadrature、重算两套恒等式、检查 bolt/collar 光滑性并准备 Arb/interval 验证；若所有 q>0 路线代价上升，则提取可辨认的 scaling law，尤其是 Z/V_w 对 T_phi−P_w 的支付。

并行检验 fixed-exterior degeneration 结论所需的最低分析输入：设计一个清晰的近极小序列场景，区分真正 stationary regularized minimizers 与任意 minimizing sequences，确定何种局部收敛足以把 compactly supported variations 传到 regular base，并用相对密度直接恢复 liminf J≥8π²q。不要重新展开逐 terminal bubble 收费；重点寻找 collapse、multi-fold 或 nonstationary limit 是否有实际低成本模型。将数值与分析发现汇总到新的 workspace/notes/ 文件，并说明它们如何改变 C1、cell conjecture 与 O11 主路线。保留非对角/MM 固定尺度构造作为独立竞争机制；若对角 q>0 搜索显示明确结构性阻碍，下一步应把该结构转化为 Agent2 可证明的 weighted Hardy/ODE 命题，而不是继续增加相似运行。
mathematical_discussion:
本步将 O11 的对角 cell 问题从笼统的数值支持推进为两个精确的补偿结构，并修正了上一轮对退化路线的判断。首先，从 I54 (6.6) 与共形 Kähler 下界逐项相减得到恒等式 J−K=A0/12+4B0+L_G/4−N(2m0−3N)/(4vK)。因此 C1 的实质是 A0、B0 与 scalar variance 的联合支付，只有 0<N<2m0/3 需要新分析；单独要求 B0 支付会人为加强问题。对一 bolt 径向模型，I55 (8.2) 给出完全等价的形式 R_rad≥q(2M0−q)/(4I_R)，其中 q=T_phi−P_w。N 与 P_w 使用不同径向权重，不能互换；scalar mean 也不能独立优化，因为 bolt-scale 共形集中可使主径向 moment 消失而把代价转移到 X、Y、Z、V_w。由此最值得证明的是保留全部 residual 的非线性 Hardy/ODE 型联合估计，而不是继续记录无约束极小值高于四。

为观察实际补偿，建立了 workspace/scripts/cell_compensation.py。它同时计算 I54 与 I55 两套精确分解，并在固定 N/m0 下最小化 j。32 个受约束运行覆盖 μ=0.1、R=2、N/m0 从 5×10^−4 到 0.55；两套恒等式的最大数值残差分别低于 6×10^−14 与 3×10^−14。所有运行均高于 C1，且 q<0，没有进入径向危险区。小目标的最佳 j−K 分别为 0.1844、0.3432、0.9804、3.236，而相应形式 gain 仅为 0.01663、0.03294、0.09796、0.3233；主要支付出现在 4B0 与 V_w。较大目标的距离快速增至约 9.89、36.05、139.41、323.02。这些有限维结果提示：低成本制造 almost-Kähler 非可积性时，inverse-weight anisotropy P_w 与 V_w/Weyl splitting 同时增长，共形梯度尚未实现 q>0 补偿。它们不是一般下界；下一次计算必须直接寻找 q>0 的实际 profile，并研究内尺度 r=√μ x 与固定外部尺度之间的耦合。

本步还发现固定外部使 noncollapsed stationary orbifold degeneration 远比一般 bubble-tree 情形刚性。若极限正则 base 的 orbifold completion 是紧致、有效、无边界且 locally CH，并保留完整外部 U=X\D 的光滑单射局部等距，则 developing maps 给出原 lattice Γ 包含于 Γ′。若 Γ′\Γ 非空，某个额外 deck transformation 必把连通无界的 lifted exterior 移入一个有界 lifted ball，与等距性矛盾；故 Γ′=Γ，base 就是原光滑 CH 曲面 X。这里完整外部与单射局部等距不可替换为一小段 collar germ。更进一步，cell 的相对恒等式 J−8π²q=∫F−4d、F=((s+3)²/3)+1+4|W+|²≥0，而 CH 上 F=4。若 fixed-collar 序列在有限点外 C²_loc 收敛到上述 stationary base，则在耗尽 D\S 的紧集上积分收敛，遗漏区域只需使用 F≥0，直接得到 liminf J≥8π²q。于是商端 ALE、eta 项与 marked topology 如何分布不再影响这一退化支的阈值；它们只在等号和精细退化分类中仍有作用。真正可能产生 subthreshold 的机制被缩到 collapse、stationarity 或 regular convergence 失效、非 orbifold/multi-fold completion、非有限集中，或真实的 smooth finite-amplitude cell。这个发现使一般正则化路线重新获得明确目标：先证明近极小序列落入已排除的 noncollapsed stationary 分支，或精确分析其余逃逸机制，而不是预先逐 terminal bubble 收取 8π²。

外部 almost-Kähler 文献提供的 harmonic-Weyl 不等式需要 δW+=0，不能直接用于任意 cell；但它提示可寻找带 δW+ 缺陷的积分恒等式，把 Weyl anisotropy 与实际 Ricci residual X、Z、V_w 相连。当前最有价值的两条互补路线因此是：在对角类中证明联合径向强制估计或找到 q>0 反 profile；在全 cell 层面利用固定外部刚性，将 compactness 问题压缩到 collapse 与非正则极限。固定尺度非对角或 Malchiodi–Malizia 型构造仍应作为否定系数四的独立检验，因为一个真正 subthreshold cell 会立即改变 balanced family 的一阶系数。O10 与固定 E_D 的达到性仍是独立核心分支，本步没有改变它们的数学状态。

research_summary:
本步创建了 `workspace/scripts/cell_qsearch.py`，以增强拉格朗日法直接约束 q=T_phi−P_w=fM0，使用 `cell_opt.py` 的精确 bolt/CH-collar 基底，并比较 inner、fixed、broad 三类初值、phi 两个符号及零/非零低模 w 初值。主要数据位于 `workspace/data/cell_qsearch/main_mu01.jsonl` 与 `workspace/data/cell_qsearch_small/musmall.jsonl`，分别含 60 和 48 个运行；`workspace/scripts/summarize_qsearch.py` 生成 `workspace/data/cell_qsearch/qsearch_best.csv`。运行覆盖 μ=.1,.03,.01、R=2、degree 22、650–750 Gauss 节点，q/M0 至少覆盖 .05–1；所有目标越过 I55 的正 q 必要下端。没有发现 j<4 或 j<K。最佳低 q 值及 residual 分解已记录；I55 直接恒等式最大误差 7.3×10^−11。固定物理初值形成约 1/μ 高成本盆地，而低成本宽基模盆地为 O(1)，但优化不保持支撑。最优解回到 w=0，因此有限幅 triaxial 机制仍未检验；q>M0 的另一半危险区也未运行。高 q 中贴近软正性层的记录没有被用于稳健数值解释。

本步读取并比较了同组会话的 rotating-eigenframe 计算 `Sessions/S1003A02/workspace/scripts/o11_rotated_cell.py`、`.../data/o11rot/summary.csv` 与 `.../notes/step6_theorems_and_O11_rotation.md`。其相对取向模量产生正的一阶成本，补充了本会话固定特征架的 q 搜索。已向消息 742 与 743 回复：locally real-hyperbolic 的 developing-map 论证可以推广，但 W+=0 的 negative Einstein base 不足以得到 real hyperbolic；一般 non-Kähler Einstein orbifold 也不能在未消除界面应力时直接排除。

独立数学核验帮助确认了 q 归一化、必要区间、数值覆盖及其不足，并提炼出内尺度命题 Rhat≥vartheta(4−vartheta)。它也明确指出 I54 的 B0 是反解量，而不是独立曲率计算；本步已在解释中修正。固定外部分析得到恢复体积公式 liminf J≥8π²Q_cell−4v_miss，并识别了 C2 匹配后仍可能存在的 (nabla_nu E)delta_Sigma 界面应力。完整推导、数据解释、缩放方程、相邻会话比较和路线更新保存在 `workspace/notes/step4_positive_q_and_recovered_volume.md`。脚本已通过 Python 编译并重跑汇总。Wolfram 本机许可过期，因此没有任何结论依赖 Wolfram 输出。当前仍未证明 C1、内尺度不等式、全 cell 阈值或 balanced 全度量系数四，也未发现 subthreshold cell。
continuation:
继续保持 Explore，以本步形成的内尺度对象为中心构造可证明的数学路线。首先从 I55 的精确 X,Y,Z,V 公式重新完成 r=sqrt(μ)x 极限，逐项核对所有系数、bolt 数据、无穷远条件及有限能量空间，明确哪些收敛假设使 J_infty=(2−vartheta)^2+Rhat 成为严格极限而非形式推导。随后攻击 Rhat≥vartheta(4−vartheta)：在 s=log x 变量中利用 Z 的 Riccati方程、V 的 anisotropy transport、X moment 与 Y scalar variance，寻找一个保留 W≠0 的加权平方完成、乘子恒等式或分区 Hardy 估计。先证明可复用的部分结果也应具有真实强度，例如有限幅 W 的某个全区间、vartheta 接近 0 或 2 的定量邻域、或者在 F 一致远离退化时覆盖 0<vartheta<4；不要回退到仅分别估计 T_phi、P_w 或 M。用现有 q 数据和 peer rotated-cell 数据检验候选常数与等号结构，但不要把离散最优值当成下界。

并行发展 fixed-exterior 分支的两个精确数学连接。其一，给出恢复区域命题的严格假设与证明，说明单值 marked C2 recovery、背景体积和 v_miss 如何定义，并研究何种非塌缩/能量条件足以推出 v_miss→0。其二，把界面应力写成自由/fixed 四阶变分问题的边界分布，判断 C3 收敛、全局弱方程、自由侧 CH 开集或 Dirichlet trace-free Einstein coercivity 中哪一种最有希望从 minimizing sequence 获得。目标是把局部比较极小性真正连接到 locally CH base，而不是再次假定跨界面唯一延拓。继续保留非 SU(2)_L fixed-scale 构造作为竞争方向：旋转模量的一阶正成本排除了一个自然机制，但一般四维 cell、非 Burns-like filler 与 q>M0 的有限幅对角分支仍可产生不同结果。把新的推导或反 profile 保存为可复用证明笔记，并说明它对 C1、cell conjecture 和 balanced coefficient-four 问题实际推进了哪一层。
mathematical_discussion:
本步首次直接进入 I55 的正 q 危险扇区，并由计算、缩放与固定外部分析共同重塑了 O11 路线。对角 cell 的精确分解为 j=(M0−q)^2/(4I_R)+R_X+R_Y+R_Z+R_V，其中 q=T_phi−P_w。新程序 cell_qsearch.py 约束 q=fM0，在 μ=.1,.03,.01、R=2 上比较 inner-scale、固定物理环带和宽基模三类延拓，并同时释放 F,w,phi。最小目标均越过 I55 对亚阈值 cell 的正 q 必要下端；因此这不再是过去未触及危险区的无约束搜索。108 个主要运行没有产生 j<4 或 j<K。代表性最佳值为 μ=.1,f=.05 时 j=7.1723、K=4.4128；μ=.03,f=.1 时 j=8.6603、K=4.1211；μ=.01,f=.1 时 j=8.4084、K=4.0401。直接 Ricci 积分与 I55 平方分解在全部运行中相差至多 7.3×10^−11。形式投影确实下降，但代价转移到 R_X、R_Z，并在 M 接近零时转入 R_Y；例如 μ=.01,f=.1 的投影仅为 3.2725，而其余项总和约 5.136。故消去主径向 moment 并不能消去实际 Einstein residual。

这些结果同时暴露了当前计算的实质空缺。最低成本解均回到 w=0；带非零 w 初值的解通常衰减到 10^−4–10^−3 幅度，P_w、N、R_V 很小。因此本步解析了正 q 的共形支付，却没有排除有限幅 triaxial 逃逸。搜索还只覆盖 0<q≤M0，而完整危险区为 0<q<2M0；投影关于 M0 对称，但非线性 residual 并无相应对称性。高 q 分支常逼近 F 的软正性层，故不能用来判断退化极限。固定物理环带初始化在小 μ 时形成 j≈C_f/μ、phi_max≈C_f′/sqrt(μ) 的高成本盆地，而宽基模盆地保持 O(1)；由于优化后未保持支撑，这说明存在不同延拓盆地，而非尺度分类定理。I54 中 B0 是由恒等式反解的记账量，其闭合不是第二套独立 Weyl 曲率计算。

缩放 r=sqrt(μ)x 将下一数学对象清晰化。若 vartheta=lim μq，则 q=fM0 对应 vartheta=2f，且内尺度能量形式为 J_infty=(2−vartheta)^2+Rhat。正确尺度、正确阈值并在 Burns 极限 vartheta=0 取等的命题是 Rhat≥vartheta(4−vartheta)，0<vartheta<4，等价于 J_infty≥4。Rhat 保留 X,Y,Z,V 的全部加权平方；在 s=log x、A=x Phi_dot、B=x W_dot 后，Z 与 V 给出耦合 Riccati/transport 系统，正好连接 signed conformal moment 与实际残量。现有数据只触及 0<vartheta≤2，且主要在 W=0 截面；真正新的部分是有限幅 W≠0 和完整区间。相邻会话独立完成的 rotating-eigenframe SU(2)_L cell 计算提供互补信息：在 x0=.003 时相对取向角从 0 到 π/2 使一阶斜率由 5.90 升到 15.20，且 4ΔW+ 与 ΔS/12 均为正。由此，Burns 与 CH Weyl 轴错位没有产生同度量负成本，反而在异常尺度的一阶付费；但部分非零角优化未完全收敛，且非 SU(2)_L 几何仍未覆盖。

固定外部路线得到一个严格的定量结论，也修正了上一轮对 stationarity 的使用。真实 J 极小序列若在自由 regular 区紧集上单值 C2 收敛，则可把任意紧支变分移植回原序列；极小性直接传递为极限的局部极小性、Euler–Lagrange 方程和稳定性，无需传递高阶正则化方程。然而这只发生在自由区内部。C2 接到固定 CH collar 仅给 E=Ric+g 在界面为零；把 E 零延拓时仍可能出现 (nabla_nu E) delta_Sigma 的界面应力。允许变分在固定开 collar 上全阶消失，不能检测该项。因此从局部 stationarity 到 locally CH base 尚需跨界面 C3 控制、无界面测度的全局弱方程、自由侧内部 CH 开集，或独立的 Dirichlet 强制估计。只有该输入建立后，唯一延拓、Einstein 解析性和 developing map 才能闭合。

另一方面，相对非负密度已足以定量描述任何亚阈值退化。若 marked CH recovery region 恢复背景体积 d−v_miss，则 F=((s+3)^2/3)+1+4|W+|^2≥0、F_CH=4 与相对恒等式给出 liminf J≥8π²Q_cell−4v_miss。因此 J≤8π²Q_cell−delta 必迫使 v_miss≥delta/4；单 blowup 的 j≤4−epsilon 对应 v_miss≥π²epsilon/2。有限点集中或任何零背景体积的 bubble tree 不能单独制造严格缺口。真正危险的是正体积 CH 恢复丢失、塌缩、多层覆盖或非 orbifold completion，而不是每个泡的拓扑收费。

Developing-map 刚性可原样推广到完整 locally real-hyperbolic orbifold：若整个删球外部以光滑单射局部等距方式嵌入，则额外 deck transformation 会把无界 lifted exterior 放入有界 lifted ball，故扩大的 lattice 不存在。但 negative Einstein 加 W+=0 并不意味着 real hyperbolic；还需 W−=0，或由真实 RH 开集、无界面应力和 Einstein 解析性传播完整常曲率张量。同理，一般 non-Kähler Einstein orbifold 加 Ricci-flat ALE fillers 不能被 O11 的 lattice 论证直接排除；先证明 regular base locally CH 仍是必要连接。综合计算与分析，最值得继续的方向不是增加相似优化，而是证明内尺度加权不等式，并并行建立恢复区域或消除界面应力的分析机制。

research_summary: Starting from the Step-4 handoff (prove R̂≥ϑ(4−ϑ)) and the Spirit note, which pointed to webvar:ae-cost, I first read the manuscript's ae-cost lemma (paper/sections/variational_selection_and_global_cost.tex lines 503–643). It gives P_N=8π²b2+32π²(b1+e−1)+4W^++S/12, and on O(−1) this yields ∫|Ric|²=8π²+4W^++S/3. I then made the topological bookkeeping explicit in the diagonal class. scripts/bianchi_transgression.py computes the Levi-Civita connection and curvature of a general diagonal Bianchi-IX coframe by Cartan's equations. It forms (1/2)εΩΩ ± ΣΩ∧Ω and solves exactly for the antiderivative G(a,b,c,a',b',c') (symbolic check = 0; output in data/transgression/G_formula.txt). transgression_values.py fixes the orientation: +1 gives T_bolt=8π² and −1 gives −40π². It also evaluates the flat (0), Taub–NUT (32π²) and Berger-cone values. transgression_cell.py converts to the cell variables and reproduces the CH collar value T=2π²R⁴=4d exactly. transgression_sign.py and transgression_triaxial.py/transgression_structure.py complete the square in c' and find the closed form T/8π²=Y²+Π. transgression_closed_form_check.py confirms it on 10⁵ random slices (max relative error 9e−14). kahler_flux_check.py shows that Y equals minus the Ricci-form potential for U(2)-Kähler slices (A/Y=−1). profile_charge.py rebuilds Step-2/4 profiles on 6001-point grids (cell_opt basis). For w=0 cells it checks the transgression against the Ricci code through conformal invariance of |W^+|²dV (max relative error 1.2e−3 from finite differences, typically 1e−5). It also confirms the inferred ∫_in F grows at least as fast as volume, and locates zero-flux slices. The results for 122 cells (108 positive-q runs and 14 sweep1 near-optimal runs) are in data/transgression/profile_charge_lines.jsonl and zero_flux_summary.json. Every converged cell has zero-flux slices, and at the best zero 8π²Π/∫_in F ≤ 0.58, so all are certified J≥8π². The first zero fails in 2 oscillating high-cost profiles (ratio 1.03). Near-optimal cells have T≈0 at r≈(2μ)^{1/4}. The figure figures/slice_charge_profiles.png (plot_slice_charge.py) shows the slice charge, inner energy and cumulative cost along four representative cells. Note notes/step5_slice_charge_and_zero_flux.md records Theorem A (slice charge), the localized identities, Theorem C (zero-flux threshold) and its corollaries, Conjecture Z, the diagonal-class proof of the inner AE threshold with the end analysis (flat 0, ALF 32π²), and the scope limitation. Peer message #746 reported that the perpendicular orientation ζ⊥ω_CH has zero first-order cost with margin O(x0²). I recorded that all our diagonal searches used the aligned slot (θ=0) and that the zero-flux certificate is unavailable in the perpendicular slot. I replied as #747 with the formula, and requested their θ=π/2 profiles so the general certificate can be evaluated on them. Sandbox notes: redirects must use literal root-relative paths, and sed -i cannot write in scripts/. No background tasks are pending.
continuation: Attack the one place where a subthreshold O11 cell is now plausible: the perpendicular orientation ζ⊥ω_CH at finite scale. (1) Build a diagonal Bianchi-IX cell optimizer in which the bolt collapses a different slot (for example σ1, a→0 with b=c at the bolt) while the exact CH collar keeps its Kähler fibre in σ3. Use the general metric form dt²+a²σ1²+b²σ2²+c²σ3², or extend cell_opt.py with slot-permuted bolt conditions. Check the O(−1) topology and orientation via T_bolt=8π² from transgression_values.py and the collar value 4d. Compare with S1003A02's scripts/o11_perp_cell.py, data/o11perp/first_order_law.csv and notes/step8_first_order_cell_law_ASD_Qprinciple.md; message #747 asks them for profiles. Determine whether their fixed-slot cells are diagonal. If they are, reproduce their θ=π/2 numbers (first-order coefficient ≈0.044 and second-order +10…21 x0²), then push to x0≈0.03–0.3 and optimize hard for J<8π². (2) On every such profile, evaluate the full slice charge T(r), the general certificate J−8π²≥Vol_in−T(Σ), and the inferred ∫_in F. A subthreshold cell must have T>∫_in F on every slice. mathematical_discussion:
This step makes the topological bookkeeping of the cell problem explicit, and finds that it splits naturally into a c1-flux part and a Kähler-defect part. For every diagonal Bianchi-IX metric dt^2+a^2σ1^2+b^2σ2^2+c^2σ3^2, the Chern–Weil form of 2χ+3τ is an exact derivative. Its antiderivative depends only on the first-order data of each slice. I computed it from the Cartan curvature and reduced it to the closed form T/(8π^2)=Y^2+Π. Here Y=c'−2cosh2w+z^2+p+p−/2 and Π=e^{2w}p+^2+e^{−2w}p−^2−(p+p−)^2/4, with e^{2w}=a/b, z=c/√(ab), p+=(ba'−c+(a^2−b^2)/c)/√(ab) and p−=(ab'−c−(a^2−b^2)/c)/√(ab). The pair p± vanishes exactly when the slice is Kähler for ω3: their sum is the closure defect and their difference the integrability defect. For U(2)-Kähler slices, Y is minus the coefficient of the Ricci-form potential. So the Chern–Weil charge of a Kähler slice is 8π² times the square of its c1-flux, which is the transgression one expects for c1²=2χ+3τ. The formula takes the correct values: 8π² at an O(−1) bolt, −40π² for the O(+1) orientation, 0 at a flat round slice, exactly 4d at the CH collar, and 32π² on Taub–NUT slices. That last value matches χ=1 and τ-density 2/3 of the self-dual Taub–NUT metric.

This gives a localized form of the inherited cell identity: J ≥ ∫_in|Ric+g|^2 = 8π^2+∫_in F − T(Σ) for every slice Σ. In the aligned class, where the bolt circle is the CH Kähler fibre σ3 (all of I54/I55 and all of our Steps 2–4), Y equals −1 at the bolt and R²/2 at the collar. A zero-flux slice therefore always exists, and at it J ≥ 8π^2+∫_in F−8π^2Π. Kähler cells thus satisfy the threshold by a one-line argument. A subthreshold aligned cell would need every zero-flux slice to be non-Kähler by more than the interior energy, ∫_in F/(8π²) ≥ Vol/(8π²). This turns the diagonal-class cell conjecture into a boundary-versus-interior statement (Conjecture Z): the Kähler defect of some zero-flux slice is bounded by the interior 4|W^+|^2+(s+3)^2/3+1. Numerically, near-optimal cells put a slice with T≈0 at r≈(2μ)^{1/4}, the Kähler crossover where −μ/r²+r²/2=0, even at μ=0.1. At the best zero of each profile the ratio 8π²Π/∫_in F is at most 0.58 across 120 cells. At the first zero the ratio can exceed 1 for oscillating high-cost profiles, so Conjecture Z should be stated as 'some zero' and not 'the first zero'.

The same identity closes the Step-4 inner-scale inequality in the diagonal class. On [1,X], ∫|Ric|^2 = 8π^2+∫(s^2/3+4|W^+|^2)−T(X) exactly. Finite curvature energy controls the logarithmic derivatives of a', b', c', because a''/a, b''/b and c''/c are sectional curvatures. Together with terminal values (1,0,Φ∞), this forces T(X_k)→0 along a sequence, so R̂−ϑ(4−ϑ)=(1/2π²)∫(ŝ²/3+4|Ŵ+|²)≥0 for finite-amplitude W and the full ϑ range. This is the inherited webvar:ae-cost identity, now with an explicit end term. The ALF value 32π² gives a concrete form of 'topology distributed across levels': collapse of the Hopf fibre in a neck moves four units of charge across it. For the cell itself, μ→0 needs only a neck slice with T=o(1); since the finite-μ identity is exact, no AE decay of the limit is needed.

Peer message #746 changes where the danger lies. S1003A02 found that the 'misalignment costs' result was an artifact. With the bolt direction perpendicular to ω_CH, the first-order cost vanishes: the Weyl saving −2x0 cancels the scalar cost +2x0, leaving a margin of order x0² (still positive in their runs). All our diagonal computations were in the aligned slot θ=0, which is the most expensive orientation. In the perpendicular slot Y is singular at the bolt, so our zero-flux certificate is unavailable there. This is consistent with the peer result: our certificate is a c1(ω_CH)-flux argument, and the orientation that evades it is the one that is free at first order. The coefficient-four question is therefore concentrated at ζ⊥ω_CH at finite x0 (about 0.03–0.3), or outside SU(2). The general certificate J−8π²≥Vol_in−T(Σ) still applies to any diagonal slot assignment.

For non-symmetric metrics the natural extension is a flux-square transgression that uses the Seiberg–Witten curvature iF_A/2π, which represents c1(L) for every metric, in place of the Ricci form. The test is whether this flux and the CH Ricci flux decouple in the perpendicular direction. None of C1, the full cell conjecture or the all-metric coefficient-four bound is proved. The new results are the slice-charge theorem, the zero-flux threshold theorem with Conjecture Z, and the closed inner AE threshold.

The certified perpendicular cell changes the governing question from whether the balanced coefficient can fall below four to what mathematical object determines collective surgery cost. Consequently \(\mathfrak J_{8,7}\le7\mathfrak J_{1,1}+\mathfrak J_{1,0}\) and \(\mathfrak J_{8,7}\le4\mathfrak J_{2,0}+224\pi^2\). Fekete subadditivity also identifies the stable fixed-cell balanced cost as \((72\pi^2)^{-1}\inf_n\mathfrak J_{8n,7n}/n\), which need not equal the one-block value. Let \(\overline J_{10}\) denote the certified smooth single-blow-up cost approached from the strict \(X=8\) enclosure, with \(\overline J_{10}/(8\pi^2)=0.999116243135324311\ldots\). A constructed two-blow-up cell improves the present balanced upper coefficient as soon as \(J_{20}<2\overline J_{10}\), yielding an improvement \((2\overline J_{10}-J_{20})/(18\pi^2)\). A blow-up--handle pair improves it if \(J_{11}<\overline J_{10}+32\pi^2\), with seven such pair savings amplified in the \((8,7)\) block. These comparisons concern certified constructions. Pure handles themselves remain rigid: \(\mathfrak J_{0,\ell}=32\pi^2\ell\), with nonattainment for fixed smooth nontrivial handle cells. Thus any handle saving must be genuinely mixed and use the blow-up-funded Weyl depletion rather than improve an isolated handle.

The proposed shared-exterior mechanism requires the fourth-order normal equation of the squared defect, not the ordinary linearized Einstein equation. At the CH metric \(g_0\), put \(E(g)=\operatorname{Ric}(g)+g\) and \(A=D E_{g_0}\). Since \(E(g_0)=0\), \(J(g_0+h)=\int|Ah|^2+O(h^3)\), and exterior minimization satisfies \(A^*Ah=0\). After Bianchi gauge fixing this is an elliptic fourth-order system, conveniently represented by \(z=A_Bh\), \(A_B^*z+\beta^*\lambda=0\), \(\beta h=0\). Its interface port is the full first jet \(q=(h,\nabla_\nu h)\), equivalently induced-metric, second-fundamental-form, marking, and gauge-compatible data; ordinary metric Dirichlet data are insufficient. Eliminating exterior variables gives a self-adjoint response form \(\Lambda^{\mathrm{ext}}\). For two ports its off-diagonal term is \(2\langle q_1,\Lambda_{12}q_2\rangle\), and a discrete implementation obtains the same object as the Schur complement \(H_{qq}-H_{qz}H_{zz}^{-1}H_{zq}\), with Jacobi and gauge modes retained separately.

Interaction does not occur while two exact CH collars remain disjoint: their defect supports then add exactly. One must cut each certified cell farther inside, retain the two actual smooth blow-up interiors, and let their genuine metric first jets share one CH exterior. If \(J_{\rm in}\) is the cost inside a chosen cut and \(J_{\rm tail}\) the discarded frozen tail, then a fixed-core pair improves two frozen witnesses precisely when the nonlinear shared-exterior cost is below \(2J_{\rm tail}\). At quadratic order the relevant quantity contains both diagonal replacement costs and the off-diagonal response; a negative cross term alone is not enough. Polarization against the two isolated one-port solves separates genuine interaction from ordinary independent tail relaxation.

Separation enters through the off-diagonal Green kernel of \(A_B^*A_B\); relative orientation acts on the transported interface jet. For the perpendicular cell, a residual \(U(1)\) phase rotates the \(\omega^\perp\) plane, so the interaction can contain invariant and weight-two parts, schematically \(I(d,\theta)=I_0(d)+2\operatorname{Re}(I_2(d)e^{2i\theta})+\cdots\). Symmetry does not automatically remove \(I_0\), because the frozen cell also has scalar and biaxial data. An orientation average vanishes only when the port or traction has no invariant component. Complex hyperbolic space is Kähler--Einstein and half-conformally flat in its complex orientation, so the sign assumptions from Malchiodi--Malizia cannot simply be transferred. Nevertheless their fourth-order gluing and Gursky--Viaclovsky's Kuranishi term \(\frac23W(z_0)\circledast W(y_0)+4tR(z_0)\operatorname{mass}\) show that position- and rotation-dependent curvature interactions are established phenomena for related quadratic functionals; the sign for \(J\) must be computed from its own scalar, Ricci, volume, and gauge terms.

The question for this step was whether two smooth blow-up cells that share one complex-hyperbolic background cost less together than apart. A cheap test was possible: take two copies of the certified cell and let their tails overlap in a trial metric. This avoids solving the relaxed-exterior problem and keeps the cores, the topology and the baseline exact. Write each cell over CH as g_B+h_i. Here h_i is diagonal in the cell's CH orthonormal coframe, with λ=((x+x²)/G, F/x, 1, e^w/(1+x)) and x=sinh²r. Then g_12=g_B+h_1+h_2 equals one cell, or CH, outside the lens L=B_ρ(0)∩B_ρ(a). So J(g_12)−2J(g_1) is exactly a lens integral. Its quadratic part is 2∫_L⟨E_1,E_2⟩, and the rest is cubic in the tail data. The construction is admissible when 0<w<ρ−r_0≈1.66, where w=2ρ−d is the overlap depth. In that range each tail vanishes near the other bolt, the topology is D#2CP̄², the exterior is exact CH, and the Step-10 O(δ³) smoothing lemma carries over to the C^{2,1} metric.

A symmetry fact organises everything. The cell defect is diagonal: radial, bolt slot, contact slot and fibre. The relative U(1) phase L_θ rotates only the contact block. The block's invariant part m=(E11+E22)/2 is fixed, and its traceless part d=(E11−E22)/2 has weight four in θ. So the quadratic interaction is exactly I_0+Re(I_4 e^{4iθ}), with minimum over phase I_0−|I_4|. A saving therefore exists for some phase as soon as the weight-four amplitude beats the orientation average.

The computation used full 4D autodiff curvature, with no symmetry assumed, and matched the Bianchi formula to 12–14 digits. Results:
- I_0 is about 1% of |I_4|.
- Best-phase savings (units of 8π², all negative): −3e-11 at w=0.1, −1.5e-7 at w=0.6, −5.3e-6 at w=1.4, −1.25e-5 at w=1.6.
- The nonlinear remainder is below 0.5% of the saving.
- The preferred phase flips near w≈0.93. This matches the single sign change of d(r) at r=1.297, since the lens is centred near r=ρ−w/2.
- As w→0 the pair repels for every phase. The collar jet e=(0.0489, 0.0946, 0, −0.0457) has zero contact-slot component (h_2≡x), so min-phase pairing is e0²+e3²+2e1e2=0.00448>0, giving I~+c w^{9/2}. The saving comes from the inner tail structure, not the collar jet.

Mechanism: beyond r>1 the cell's defect is about 90% weight-two (1.80e-4 against 1.87e-5 for the invariant part). This is the ω⊥ perpendicular anisotropy identified in Steps 7–8. The scalar and fibre parts are nearly paid off.

The key judgement is about size. The best pair saving is 1.4% of η_8=8.84e-4 and 0.2% of the Cauchy–Schwarz scale ∫_L|E_1|². If certified, it would lower the balanced coefficient by only about 5e-6, through 𝔍_{8,7}≤4𝔍_{2,0}+224π². Going from X=8 to X=16 for a single cell improves the deficit seventeen times more (Δη=2.1e-4). So explicit cost is not additive, which is now numerically established for frozen cells, but separated optimised cells interact only weakly. Optimisation pushes more than 99.9% of the defect into the core, and frozen-tail interaction is limited by the tail energies.

Three possibilities remain for collective savings comparable to η:
- (a) Many phase-aligned neighbours per cell. Hyperbolic packing at d≈1.9 allows many. The open question is frustration of the phase field around triangles, plus triple overlaps.
- (b) A jointly relaxed exterior. This is the stronger Dirichlet-to-Neumann problem. Its gain over frozen tails is plausibly also limited by tail energy.
- (c) Genuine core–core cooperation at distances below ρ+r_0. There the tail representation fails, and a cohomogeneity-two ansatz is needed, for example toric iterated blow-ups.

So the main lever for the upper bound is still the single-cell infimum κ1=𝔍_{1,0}/8π² and its large-collar limit. The weight-two phase law is a reusable structural fact for any cluster or mixed-cell construction. Peer S1003A02 found that diagonal SU(2) Einstein fillings of D#CP̄² are ACH with Rossi-sphere ratio ≥2.196, never standard. That links directly to whether κ1 is bounded below within the ansatz. The central middle-scale problem is now sharply identified: control the full spin moment M_\Phi=-1-2\int\sum_i p_iH_i/\lambda_i and its weighted norm, jointly with the two shape moments, over a compact bolt-scale regime. A localized state-function identity offers a route: for B_i^{\eta,F}=\eta a_iF_{u_i}/W, \langle z,B^{\eta,F}\rangle_W=[\eta F]_0^T-\int\eta'F-2\int\eta\sum_iF_{u_i}H_i/\lambda_i. The core–exterior reduction remains the most informative representation of the diagonal cell problem, but this step changed what numerical stationarity means and repaired the large-collar values. The exact CH antisymmetric exterior has terminal cost E_ext=δ²/I, with δ=-2k(ρ)Θ-w₀G(ρ), and its costate convention is λ=-δ/I. The off-null response has w=A-2λ log x+o(1), while the torsion relation gives θ=(λ/2)x^{-2}log x+O(x^{-2}); the logarithm omitted in the earlier asymptotic description is essential. A nonzero λ is compatible with negligible scalar defect because the antisymmetric CH linearization has δs=0. Thus a limiting branch can have J₆-P→0 while retaining trace-free far-field stress.

The inherited conformal variation supplies an independent structural equation. In Ric=-6 normalization, for e=s+24,
δJ₆[2fg]=4∫f(Δ₊+6)e. A smooth complete finite-J₆ critical limit admitting compactly supported conformal variations must therefore satisfy e=0 by cutoff testing, so J₆=P. This does not imply Einstein and does not force λ=0. Conversely, a smooth full critical cell with an open exact-CH collar cannot exist: e vanishes first, the tensor Euler equation and unique continuation force Ric=-6g everywhere, and the resulting locally CH topology contradicts the exceptional sphere. Hence the numerical branch should be understood as an infinite-ended or nonattained variational object, not as a smooth fixed-collar critical cell.

mathematical_discussion:
This step changed what the diagonal cell programme can establish. There were three findings.

First, the scalar channel has been removed exactly, not by penalty. In four dimensions any conformal change ĝ=u²g satisfies ŝ²dV̂=(s−6Δu/u)²dV pointwise. Conformal invariance of |W|²dV and of the Gauss–Bonnet Pfaffian, modulo a transgression, then give the following. If ĝ has constant scalar curvature −κ, then P(g)−P(ĝ)=κ∫|∇u|²+3∫(Δu/u)². For κ=24 one gets J₆(g)−J₆(ĝ)=∫[3(Δu/u)²+24|∇u|²+e²/4]. Equivalently 3(Δu/u)²=(e+24(u²−1))²/12. So the constant-scalar representative is the unique minimizer of both J₆ and P in its conformal class.

On closed negative-Yamabe manifolds this is an exact form of the inherited inequality δ=S(g)−S(ĝ)≥0. In s=−4 normalization, δ=48∫|∇u|²+36∫(Δu/u)². Combined with inherited (3.10), this gives the following for every E-minimizing sequence: the normalized H¹ energy and ∫(Δu/u)² of the conformal factors to the Yamabe metrics tend to zero. That is quantitative conformal-factor control, which the inherited text lists as missing. It still gives no geometric compactness.

For cells the infinite-ended version needs three inputs. (1) Existence: for s<0 everywhere, constant sub- and supersolutions and exhaustion give a solution u. (2) Decay: u−1=O(e^{−(2+2√3)r}), from m²+4m−8=0 and CH volume growth e^{4r}. (3) Truncation: truncating back to an exact collar costs O(e^{(4−2m)R}). Then inf J₆ over s<0 cells equals inf P over complete CH-asymptotic metrics with s≡−24. This holds inside the diagonal and SU(2) ansätze as well. A subtle point remains open: 6λ₀(CH²)+s_CH=0, so the conformal Laplacian of CH sits exactly at the bottom of its spectrum. Existence of u→1 for cells with s≥0 somewhere therefore needs its own argument. Only cells with s<0 are reduced.

The numerical gain of the Yamabe correction is tiny: 4.6e−7 at X=128 and 4.4e−8 at X=512. That gain is about 4/3 of the scalar energy, which shows the residual scalar defect of the spectral cells is high-frequency noise. The value is structural, and it holds for all metrics: the lower theory needs only P under the constraint s=−24.

Second, symmetry breaking within SU(2) does not help. The full non-diagonal SU(2)-invariant J₆ Hessian at the converged x₀=.038 cells has these properties:
- The three channels are decoupled by Z₂×Z₂ sign flips (off-block entries <1e-13, gradient ~1e-11).
- Generalized eigenvalues converge to strictly positive values: 80.13, 260.65 and 462.25 at X=512.
- The bolt twist toward the CH fibre has stiffness 0.605.
- The (1,2) rotation tends to the exact U(1) zero mode, which is the same phase symmetry seen in the pair-interaction law I(θ).

The diagonal branch is therefore a strict local minimum among SU(2)-invariant metrics modulo U(1). The coherent picture is that the SU(2)-diagonal value near 0.99517 is locally optimal in its symmetry class. Any further constructive decrease of the cell cost must come from non-SU(2) modes (higher Peter–Weyl isotypes). A different mechanism is also possible: mixed topology, or multi-core/shared-exterior effects that are inherently non-SU(2). This bears directly on the goal of optimal constants: it says where improvement can and cannot come from.

Third, the scalar constraint turns the diagonal Hamilton–Jacobi problem into a constrained-control problem. Since s=Λ−2Σz with Λ=−8Σa_iH_i/W, admissible controls lie on the affine plane Σz=(Λ+24)/2. The subsolution condition weakens from H_S≤0 to H_S≤(W/12)(c−Σζ)². The seed −kΦ still fails along the witness, because the slack vanishes on a hypersurface. A genuine certificate needs S redesigned, for example with Λ-dependence chosen so that the slack stays positive on the u₂≈2 failure band.

Taste judgment: within the diagonal class the upper side is saturated, and the lower side is a hard 6-dimensional HJ problem whose result would only cover that restricted class. The highest-value next decisions are as follows.
(a) Test non-SU(2) stability through the isotypic Hessian with the diffeomorphism gauge quotiented. This decides whether the diagonal value is even a local unrestricted optimum.
(b) If it is stable, pursue the constrained HJ or another lower route, and the global and mixed branches.

\[
u_-=0\ \text{inside }R,\qquad u_-=1-e^{-a(r-R)}\ \text{outside},
\]
\[
u_+=M\ \text{inside }R,\qquad u_+=1+(M-1)e^{-a(r-R)}\ \text{outside}
\]
satisfy \(-6\Delta u_-+su_-+24u_-^3\le0\) and the reverse inequality for \(u_+\). Their normal-derivative jumps have the required distributional signs: \(+a\) for the lower barrier produces a nonpositive contribution to \(-6\Delta u_-\), while \(-a(M-1)\) for the upper barrier produces a nonnegative contribution. Ordered iteration on compact exhaustions, after a fixed positive shift making the nonlinearity monotone on \([0,M]\), gives a global solution of
\[
-6\Delta u+su+24u^3=0,\qquad u\to1.
\]
The strong maximum principle propagates positivity through the core, and the resulting conformal metric \(\widehat g=u^2g\) is complete with scalar curvature \(-24\). The construction bypasses the spectral threshold of the conformal Laplacian at the zero solution because the lower barrier is positive on the end and may vanish only in the compact core.

The solution is unique. If two factors exist, their quotient \(w\to1\) satisfies \(-6\Delta w-24w+24w^3=0\) relative to one normalized metric; interior maxima above one and minima below one contradict the equation. Uniqueness also preserves every end-preserving symmetry of the input metric.

On the exact end, \(v=u-1\) satisfies \(-6\Delta v+48v+72v^2+24v^3=0\). Comparison with \(e^{-mr}\) gives \(|\nabla^k v|=O(e^{-mr})\) for every fixed \(k\) and every \(m<2+2\sqrt3\), because the indicial expression is \(-m^2+4m+8\). Selecting \(4<m<2+2\sqrt3\) is decisive: the Pfaffian transgression and the integration-by-parts flux contain terms linear in \(u-1\) or \(\nabla u\), so their boundary integrals decay as \(e^{(4-m)r}\), not merely as a quadratic \(e^{(4-2m)r}\). \[

\[

Consequently d_m is proportional to A_m and supplies far more insertion sites than required when Q_m=o(A_m). The strict inequality A_m<3χ also distinguishes these compact Kähler–Einstein surfaces from compact ball quotients. Their positive canonical class is ample, so they are minimal surfaces of general type. The canonical Seiberg–Witten structure therefore supplies the same metricwise polarized input used by the inherited linear-window theorem, and the exceptional-sign selection and handle loop insertions remain available after surgery.

For M_m=\bar X_m#k_m\overline{CP}²#ℓ_m(S¹×S³), direct characteristic-number algebra gives T_+=A_m−k_m−4ℓ_m and T_−=A_m/3+4Δ_m/3+5k_m−4ℓ_m. The lower dependence on the background Chern defect \(\Delta\) cannot be exploited at first order merely by modifying a ramification region far from the surgery. Let \(t=(4\ell-5k)/A=h(1-6\theta)\), \(S_0=32\pi^2A\), and \(B_\Delta=8\pi^2\Delta/3\). For a metric whose surgery lies in \(U\) and whose topology-preserving background modification lies in a disjoint region \(N\), with exact Kähler--Einstein matching annuli, the numerator of
\[
\mathcal E-\frac{4t}{1+t}
\]
obeys
\[
\mathcal N\ge-16B_U^0-48tB_N^0
+\frac{1-3t}{3}\bigl(S(g_1)-S_0\bigr)
+4(1-3t)P_N+(1+t)L_s(g).
\]
Here \(g_1\) restores \(N\) to the KE background, \(B_U^0,B_N^0\) are the original background \(W^-\)-energies, and \(P_N\) is the trace-free Ricci energy of the topology-preserving modification. The proof uses the exact local relation \(P_N=\delta S_N/12+4\delta B_N\), the closed actual-field scalar estimate \(S(g_1)\ge S_0\), and retention of the global nonnegative scalar variance \(L_s(g)\). No comparison among three separate scalar variances is needed. For \(0\le t\le1/3\), \(B_U^0=o(Q)\), and \(\Delta/A\to0\), this gives
\[
\mathcal E(g)\ge\frac{4t}{1+t}-o(h)=4h(1-6\theta)-o(h),
\]
even when \(\Delta/Q\to\infty\). Thus separated ramification depletion cannot alter the first-order cost in this class. The result is restricted to \(\theta\le1/6\), exact KE interfaces, and a separable geometry; it does not cover the balanced \(\theta=2/9\) branch or arbitrary competitors.

The same algebra explains why local characteristic transgression alone has no sign. On a topology-preserving ramification neighbourhood with the same outer germ as the KE metric,
\[
\delta B_N=\frac14P_N-\frac1{48}\delta S_N,
\]
and, after scalar normalization to \(s=-4\),
\[
\delta B_N=\frac14P_N-\frac13\delta V_N.
\]
Consequently anti-self-dual depletion is exactly a local volume--Ricci exchange: it occurs when the relative volume increase exceeds \(3P_N/4\). The separated theorem works because the closed restored metric supplies a global scalar estimate and the ramification contribution is multiplied by \(t=O(h)\), not because a local retention inequality has been proved. Any genuine first-order \(r\)-dependence must therefore come from surgery that overlaps the non-complex-hyperbolic cap geometry, or from a global deformation that cannot be split across KE annuli.

The exact Calabi cap is correspondingly the right new local geometry. After \(\tau=\tau_0u\), \(X=\sqrt{\tau_0}x\), \(Y=\sqrt{\tau_0}y\), and \(\Psi=\tau_0\psi\), it becomes the universal pointed metric
\[
g_C=u(dX^2+dY^2)+\frac{du^2}{q(u)}+q(u)(d\Psi+X\,dY)^2,
\qquad q(u)=\frac23(u^2-u^{-1}),\quad u\ge1,
\]
with \(\Psi\)-period \(2\pi\). Ramification enters through the horizontal quotient lattice rather than the pointed formula. Its curvature reservoir satisfies \(|W^-|^2=8/(3u^6)\), divisor area \(2\pi e\), and total energy \(8\pi^2e/3\); the slab \(1\le u\le L\) captures exactly the fraction \(1-L^{-4}\). This gives a concrete finite-amplitude environment in which to seek a non-Kähler blow-up or handle cell with a Calabi outer collar.

Source reading corrected an important extrapolation. Biquard--Guenancia prove smooth convergence on compact subsets away from the divisor, which supports the established CH-site transfer, and prove order-zero ratio-one comparison with the Calabi model near the divisor. Their introduction explicitly distinguishes this negative-case result from all-derivative control. Thus their displayed results do not yet give curvature-level convergence on moving cap regions, actual concentration of \(B_\Delta\) in fixed physical cap slabs, or \(\Theta(\Delta)\) embedded fixed-radius cap sites. A transfer theorem needs uniform ramified local charts, a \(C^{2,\alpha}\) or stronger upgrade from the KE/Monge--Ampère equation, and arithmetic control of the normalized horizontal systole. Divisor area and self-intersection alone do not prevent thin tori. Hill's Heisenberg-lattice description, Bergström--van der Geer's explicit cusp matrices, Džambić's index and self-intersection formulas, and newly retrieved cone-regularity sources identify the ingredients but do not yet complete this bridge.

Peer A02 supplied a complementary global mechanism. On a fixed blow-up complex structure every Kähler metric has \(P>8\pi^2k\), whereas the certified perpendicular cell is non-Kähler and its compatible almost-Kähler form has zero exceptional period. Paired sign monopoles recover the exceptional class through a relative line bundle, but their spinor pairing may vanish by relative spin-direction rotation rather than amplitude loss. A covariant rotation or vortex estimate remains absent. This explains why a purely Kähler cap ansatz is scientifically weak and why a non-Kähler cap construction and a paired-field lower theory are genuinely complementary.

The most valuable constructive alternatives are now distinct. One is a symmetry-breaking spin-two response calculation for the certified cell forced by the cap's \(W^-\), followed if useful by a finite-amplitude toric Riemannian cap cell. Another is a divisor-localized field identity or paired-field rotation estimate. Malchiodi--Malizia and Gursky--Viaclovsky provide chiral Weyl contractions and biharmonic gluing structures, but their Weyl-energy terms do not by themselves determine \(\int|\operatorname{Ric}+g|^2\); scalar and volume channels must remain in every comparison. The target for a cap blow-up is to beat the certified CH cost \(8\pi^2\times0.995670030355131\), not merely \(8\pi^2\). The broader unrestricted blow-up cost, mixed cells, collapse, density-free O10, and Dehn-twist attainment remain central and unresolved; the ramified towers have bounded \(\chi/A\) and do not probe O10's diverging-density regime.

In that chart the transported full cell costs 1.916. Binning the excess by angle shows that the large tail part (0.74 for r>2) sits in normal-leaning directions, away from D'. where e is the Euler density and l the signature density. Relative to a fixed background, the characteristic-form terms are exact. Their S³-averaged transgression is analytic in (y = r², z = ε/r²). This was verified as a rational-function identity in sympy for the H²×H² Weyl jet, and extended to all W⁻ by equivariance and irreducibility. The verifier also supplied a clean first-variation flux argument for the order-ε term: ℓ = −R⁺_p(ζ,ζ). Together, the logarithmic saving P/8π² = 1 − 9ε²log(1/ε) + O(ε²) belongs to the R⁺-kernel orientation at any point of any negative KE surface, not to complex-hyperbolic geometry. mathematical_discussion:
This Step turned the Step-50 general-KE logarithmic Burns saving into a formula covering the full spectrum of R⁺. Conditional on the two-scale remainder theorem, which is still unwritten, it identifies exactly where the mechanism saves energy and where it does not.

Notation: s is scalar curvature, λ_ζ = W⁺(ζ,ζ), μ_ζ = R⁺(ζ,ζ) = λ_ζ + s/12, T is the trace-free part of R⁺ on ζ^⊥, and |T|² = (μ₁−μ₂)²/2. The perpendicular Burns corner coefficient is
F = −μ_ζ(μ_ζ − s/8) − |T|²,
with zero coefficient for W⁻ and for Ric°. This agrees with A02's Theorem 57.Φ (#831), which A02 obtained in conformal coordinates and checked on product backgrounds. I obtained it by an independent method in normal coordinates, using only the curvature 2-jet.

Method. The key fact is a homogeneity identity: for g = δ + a h₂ + ε(k_B + a k₀), the CGB density satisfies f(a,ε;λx) = λ⁻⁴ f(aλ², ελ⁻²; x). Hence the degree −4 part of the order-ε² density is exactly the a²ε² Taylor coefficient at |x| = 1. No Laurent extraction is needed, and only h₂ = −(1/3)R_{ikjl}x^kx^l enters. Using h₂ alone, this reproduces Step 49's full-background Ric°-form numbers exactly: 12 for k_B only on CH, 17.6 on H²×H², and −18 for both optima. That is a direct test of the Step-50 claim that higher jets enter only through exact forms.

So far the reduction is established by computation, not by a written proof. Every run also returned a pointwise-zero diagonal [aε] coefficient, so no ε log ε term appears, as the ASD and scalar-flat Burns structure predicts.

Exact part. Where T = 0 and ζ is an eigenvector, the jet is U(2)_ζ-invariant. Averaging over the compact group reduces the optimum to four invariant correctors, and the integrand is constant on S³. Sympy then gave
F_opt(s, λ_ζ) = (s − 24λ)(s + 12λ)/288,
identical to Φ. The Hessian is PSD with eigenvalues 13/2 ± √73/2, 0, 0, so this is the true invariant minimum. At the kernel point λ = −s/12 the value is 0.

On the kernel locus, F is a U(2)_ζ-invariant quadratic form in Rm_p, and T has U(1)_+ weight 2. These two facts force F = αs² + β|T|² with no cross term. The exact sympy value gives α = 0, and the inherited Ch.5 value F = −18 at KE (|T|² = 18 at s = −24) gives β = −1. Hence F = −|T|² exactly on the whole kernel interval, modulo the Ch.5 input. The floating sweep F = −2(w+1)² (to 1e-14) independently checks the quadratic-form reduction.

Interpretation. The logarithmic saving equals the defect of W⁺ from being Hermitian-type with respect to Burns's own complex structure J_ζ. A perpendicular KE insertion is the extreme case, because ω ∈ ζ^⊥ splits the perpendicular block maximally. The saving vanishes only for W⁺ = (|s|/12, s/24, s/24) with ζ the simple top eigenvector. By Derdziński, this is the pointwise curvature type of Einstein metrics conformal to a Kähler metric whose Kähler form is ζ.

Consequences for the attainment chain (A02 53.B/D/E), via bubble movement, conditional on the remainder theorem and on energy equality:
- excluded: bulk points where some R⁺(ζ,ζ) > 0 (first-order saving), and kernel points with T ≠ 0 (log saving);
- surviving: points with R⁺ < 0 strictly, where Burns genuinely pays ε|μ_ζ| at first order, and degenerate Hermitian-type kernel points, where an ε² analysis is needed.
Therefore any surviving bulk has λ_max(W⁺) ≤ |s|/12 everywhere, so |W⁺|² ≤ s²/24 with equality excluded.

I checked by hand that LeBrun's Weyl estimate together with Gauss–Bonnet does not exclude an Einstein bulk with t = √6|W⁺|/|s| ≤ 1/2 when c₁² = A: the pointwise polynomial 1/4 + 2t − 5t² is nonnegative on [0, 1/2]. The R⁺ < 0 branch is therefore a genuine global problem, not a hidden remainder.

The pointwise threshold t = 1/2 reappears as a minimizer constraint, so excluding it needs a differential or global input: the δW⁺ = 0 Weitzenböck identity, Gursky-type inequalities, SW curvature estimates, or finite-scale surgery. mathematical_discussion:
This Step turned the general-background perpendicular Burns saving into a theorem for any Einstein metric at a kernel point. It also showed exactly where the local mechanism helps and where it does not.

The theorem rests on three structural facts, each now exact or proved.

(1) Symmetry. When W⁻_p = Ric°_p = 0, every ingredient is SU(2)₋-equivariant: the 2-jet, k_B, and correctors built from x and the J_m x. SU(2)₋ acts simply transitively on S³, so the corner density is constant on the sphere. The full infimum problem therefore reduces to a 10-dimensional space of invariant correctors sym(v_i v_jᵀ)/u, which spans all invariant degree-0 symmetric tensors. Convexity plus Haar averaging, over an averaging-closed class, makes this the full answer in the (s, W⁺) sector. Exact rational polarization gives:
- F_opt = −μ_ζ(μ_ζ − s/8) − |T|² for any eigenvector ζ, which is A02's Φ, now exact;
- Spirit's explicit kernel family is the exact minimizer, with F = −|T|² and zero gradient.
So the Ch.5 value −18 is a consequence, not an input.

(2) Representation theory plus compatibility. W⁻ cross terms vanish by spin-2 irreducibility. The W⁻ self-term vanishes pointwise by the Step-50 identity. Hence no W⁻ smallness is needed.

(3) Order-ε flux. The odd jets are killed by antipodal parity, because x ↦ −x preserves orientation in dimension 4. At an Einstein metric the order-ε term is the inner-boundary flux of the Chern–Weil transgression, since D|Ric°|² = 0 there. TTCS supplied the direct computation θ₂ = 8π²μ_ζ: Burns is Kähler, its Λ⁺-connection variation is L_ζ r⁻²η, and this pairs with F⁺ through R⁺(ζ,ζ). So the first-order term is exactly −8π²εR⁺(ζ,ζ).

Together: for an eigenvector ζ,
(P − P(g) − 8π²)/8π² = −με + ½[−μ(μ − s/8) − |T|²] ε² log(1/ε) + O(ε²).
On the kernel this gives P(g_ε) = P(g) + 8π² − 4π²|T|² ε² log(1/ε) + O(ε²).

The saving is the defect of R⁺ from J_ζ-Hermitian type on ζ^⊥. It needs no complex-hyperbolic or Kähler–Einstein collar, only a kernel direction with T ≠ 0.

The mixed-block result is a genuine new phenomenon. If ζ is not an eigenvector, the corrector sym(x⊗J₂x)/u, the gauge of a rotation growing like log r, is a Hessian-null direction with a linear coupling. The log coefficient is then unbounded below: rotating the Burns orientation along the neck harvests the gradient of μ(ζ). This is consistent, because such ζ come with first-order savings anyway (once μ_ζ = 0 is imposed). It says that the ε² log order is meaningful only at critical orientations.

Outside the ansatz-level savings, three cases survive:
(i) R⁺ < 0, which pays at first order — for example real hyperbolic metrics;
(ii) s < 0 with W⁺ of degenerate type (−s/12, s/24, s/24);
(iii) R⁺ = 0.
Lemma 52.C removes open sets of (ii) on Einstein metrics: δW⁺ = 0 makes the simple eigenform parallel, which contradicts the Kähler eigenvalue s/6.

So the local mechanism closes off everything except a strictly negative cone with possibly isolated contact. That remaining branch is global. It is exactly Problem 1's missing distribution information: t = √6|W⁺|/|s| ≤ 1/2, with |W⁺|² < s²/24 strictly. Excluding non-KE Einstein bulk there needs genuinely global or differential input — Gursky-type W⁺ inequalities, SW curvature estimates using the actual basic class, or rigidity — not more local expansion.

This tells us where to invest next. The local constructive theory for Problems 2 and 3 is now essentially complete at this order for Einstein backgrounds. Remaining local items are non-Einstein bulk (the Ric° corrector and the DP term) and the EH analogue. A02 is taking the EH analogue. The high-value open centres are:
- the global R⁺ < 0 branch, linking Problem 3 attainment to Problem 1 existence;
- Problem 4 Goldberg, still untouched since Step 48.

The EH insight passed to A02 is that EH has 𝒞 ≡ 0, like Burns. The λ⁴ coefficient is therefore again a minimized square up to fluxes, and the dangerous term is an inner flux of order λ². This parallels Biquard's obstruction det R⁺ = 0, the EH analogue of our kernel condition R⁺ζ = 0.

mathematical_discussion:
This Step did two things. It closed the last numerical-only local sector of the Burns corner theory with a structural proof. It also built a decisive test for Problem 4: is negative-scalar Goldberg a local or a global problem?

(1) The Ric° corrector, Lemma 53.1. The Step-52 least-squares fit was non-unique (rank 12 of 17), and its rationalized coefficients were spurious. Both facts are now explained. The pure-Ric° normal 2-jet is exactly gauge plus conformal: h_E = 2fδ + L_Vδ, with f = −q/4 and V = −uEx/12 + qx/6. Burns g_ε = δ + εk_B is exactly ASD and scalar-flat, and f_ε = f − εq_H/(8u) is g_ε-harmonic to first order. W⁺ is conformally covariant and natural, and on a scalar-flat metric s' = −6Δf. So the variation L_Vg_ε + 2f_εg_ε preserves (W⁺, s) = 0 to first order. Its ε-coefficient
  k₀^E = L_Vk_B − (q/2)k_B − (q_H/4u)δ
is therefore an exact corrector of degree 0. Exact rational-point checks confirm it for two unrelated E: all 7 components vanish and the source is nonzero. Dropping the q_H term breaks only the scalar component, as conformal covariance predicts.

The Gauss–Bonnet/signature identity P = ∫(4|W⁺|² + s²/12) − 8π²(2χ+3τ) holds for every metric. Combined with it, the ε²log corner coefficient F = −μ_ζ(μ_ζ − s/8) − |T|² now has closed-form proofs of zero W⁻ and zero Ric° contribution, with no Einstein hypothesis in the corner computation itself. For non-Einstein (P-critical) bulk, two things remain: the order-ε bulk variation, and the claim that higher jets enter only through exact forms (proved via Einstein in Step 50). Lemma 52.C does not transfer, because it uses δW⁺ = 0. This is where A02's Part A should take over.

(2) Goldberg. The AAD local-rigidity source (read this Step) states three things:
- all known local strictly AK Einstein metrics (Nurowski–Przanowski, Tod) are Ricci-flat with W⁻ = 0 and η = 0;
- AK Einstein metrics with ω an eigenform of W⁺ are of NPT type, hence Ricci-flat and noncompact;
- the negative case is wide open.
So local existence for λ < 0 with q > 0 is not supplied by the literature found so far (the knowledge request was partial). This makes local versus global the decisive question. A finite-order prolongation obstruction would prove Goldberg locally, and hence globally. Formal compatibility would show that a global mechanism is required.

Counting the system (12 unknown functions − 4 gauge versus 14 equations − 5 identities) shows it is overdetermined by one function. Even so, the number of free top-order coefficients is free_D ≈ −D³/6 + 3D², positive until about degree 18. Pure counting forces nothing at accessible orders, so any obstruction must appear as a nontrivial syzygy: a Jacobian rank below the trivial-identity bound B_D.

The new JAX jet engine reproduces the exact H²×H² KE jet with residual 0. At D = 4, KE, Ricci-flat strictly AK and λ < 0 strictly AK (q(0) = 0.3) jets all exist, with rank equal to B_4 and with η(0), W⁻(0) and the W⁺ spectrum generic. This is consistent with the source, since the special NPT structure is not forced at low order even for λ = 0. Degrees 5–7 are running.

The closed canonical form β = iF_𝒜 − (s/4)ω has β∧β = |η|²vol pointwise, because β − η = ±a∧Ja is decomposable. It re-derives the AK balance as [β]² = ∫|η|². Hodge comparison gives the new lower bound ∫q²/16 ≥ 8π²‖c₁^{−,h}‖²: nonintegrability is forced to pay for any anti-self-dual harmonic part of c₁. That is a genuine but one-sided relation; the upper direction, which forces q = 0, still needs new input.

If the jet tower shows syzygies that constrain η(0) or q(0) at λ < 0 but not at λ = 0, that would be a major local mechanism. If not, the research must turn to global inputs. Candidates are:
- the β-Hodge structure together with the Step-48 Weyl–Bochner identity (still to be verified symbolically);
- SW theory, where η is exactly the obstruction to the Taubes configuration (f·1, A + 2i d^c log f) solving the curvature equation. Its (0,2) part reads η = −2(dd^c log f)^{anti}, a torsion contraction of d log f. Whether actual SW solutions force such a representation is a concrete actual-field question.

So the kernel and cokernel of A_N are universal across KE, RF and NEG, and across every value of q0/|λ|. An integrability condition is a polynomial G_ℓ(j_low; λ) = ℓ·b_N for a left-null vector ℓ of A_N that the known identities do not generate. A projection that vanishes identically is a hidden identity; a nonzero one on generic lower jets is a genuine condition. This makes Spirit #63's criterion precise.

It also shows that the Step-53 test is blind to the thing it was meant to detect. A genuine condition contributes a nonzero row ∇G acting on the lower variables, so the full Jacobian keeps the trivial rank B_D. Only hidden identities or singular points lower that rank. Meanwhile Levenberg–Marquardt at degree D satisfies any condition arising up to D by moving the lower coefficients. So 'rank = B_4' at D = 4, and any convergence at D = 5–7, only show that D-jets exist.

(2) Exact counting forces integrability conditions by degree 15. The trivial cokernel at degree N has three parts:
- E1 is algebraic with rank 4 per monomial. Writing J = g⁻¹ω, one has J²+1 = (1−|a+|²−|a−|²)I + 2A+A−, whose linearisation has rank 1+3. The other 6 directions are products of lower anti-self-dual parts, which vanish once the lower orders hold. That gives 6n_N.
- d∘d = 0 gives n_{N−2}.
- The contracted Bianchi identity gives 4n_{N−3}.
Hence the involutive-count rank is rank_inv = 4n_N + 4n_{N−1} + 9n_{N−2} − 4n_{N−3}, with n_d = C(d+3,3). The gauge (vector fields of degree N+1) puts 4n_{N+1} into the kernel. The free count f(N) = 12n_N − 4n_{N−1} − 9n_{N−2} + 4n_{N−3} − 4n_{N+1} is, for N = 2..15:
15, 28, 42, 56, 69, 80, 88, 92, 91, 84, 70, 48, 17, −24.
The Darboux gauge (ω = ω0 fixed, g = g0 exp(H), H symmetric and anticommuting with J0, Hamiltonian gauge n_{N+2}) gives the same numbers via 6n_N − 10n_{N−2} + 4n_{N−3} − n_{N+2}; checked by hand at N = 2, 3, 14, 15.
Since the gauge lies inside the kernel, f(15) < 0 means A_15 has at least 24 cokernel directions beyond the trivial ones. Genuine conditions or hidden identities must therefore first appear at some N1 ≤ 15, not near 18 as Step 53 estimated.
The local question becomes a finite Cartan–Kuranishi completion. The system is real-analytic (Einstein metrics are analytic in harmonic coordinates, and so is the harmonic form ω), so the outcomes are decisive:
- an inconsistent completion on the branch λ<0, q>0 proves local, hence global, negative Goldberg;
- an involutive completion gives local analytic strictly AK Einstein metrics with λ<0 by Cartan–Kähler, which would be new, since all known local examples are Ricci-flat;
- a restricted family of solutions shrinks the global problem to classifying that family's compact members.

(3) Controls and constraints already known locally.
- The exact H2×H2 KE jet extends to all orders.
- An explicit Ricci-flat strictly AK control follows from AAD's local models (48)–(50) with u = 0: g = w(dx²+dy²+dz²) + w⁻¹(dt + v dz)², with h = w + iv holomorphic in x+iy (for example h = 1 + c(x+iy)). Cauchy–Riemann gives d(v dz) = *dw, so this is Gibbons–Hawking with harmonic V = w and is hyperkähler for I. The opposite structure J has Ω = w dx∧dy − dz∧dt, which is closed and strictly AK wherever dw ≠ 0 (Tod's examples). Such jets must pass every λ = 0 condition; generic RF jets need not.
- The local exclusions as cited in the sources: η = 0 forces NPT type and Ricci-flatness (Armstrong, via AAD); nonflat constant curvature carries no AK structure even locally (Blair 1990, via Lejmi–Upmeier).
- So local λ<0 solutions need η ≠ 0. The W+ = 0 branch, where Weitzenböck forces q = (2/3)|s| constant and exactly saturates AK balance (for example reversed-orientation CH²), is excluded locally.
- Under rescaling, q/|λ| is the invariant parameter, so several values must be tested.

(4) A representation for the global problem. AAD's canonical Chern form γ_J = R(Ω) − a∧Ja = −db is iF of the Blair (first canonical) connection. It agrees with Step 53: β = γ_J − (s/4)ω, β+ = η + (q/8)ω, β− = −(q/8)ω̂. Taghavi-Chabert's Proposition 4.2 says an AK metric is Einstein iff ∇̊^γ N_{γ(αβ)} = 0 and Ric̊_{αβ̄} − N_{αδγ}N_β̄^{δγ} = Λh. Together with η = −½div¹(A), the first derivative of the Nijenhuis section is then governed by a canonically twisted Dirac-type operator whose two components are 0 (the Einstein condition) and η. The natural global identity is its Weitzenböck formula with the full canonical curvature (including η and the transverse part) and the torsion N, which is exactly what Problem 4 asks to retain. It parallels the corpus O10 torsion identity (L−2)t = D*Dt + (Γ−R−1)t.
My reading of AAD (47) specialised to Einstein (Ric'' = 0, ρ0 = 0, A_Z = 0) is: ∇*∇(∇Ω) + (3s/4)∇Ω = terms in d(κ−s), δW3+ and ρ*'' ~ η. For s<0 this is a Helmholtz equation with the wrong sign. That would be the local reason integral identities fail (compare Step 48's −(3/32)s²q), and it locates the decisive information in either the overdetermination (degree ≤ 15) or global topology (β-Hodge, Seiberg–Witten). This reading is unverified.

Judgement: the symbol and cokernel computation up to degree 15 is cheap, exact and decisive for the local side of Problem 4, and should precede any larger degree ladder. The canonical-Dirac Bochner identity is the matching global route.

∇*∇(∇Ω)_X+(3s/4)∇_XΩ=[dq_X/2−2⟨(δW₃⁺)_{JX},Ω⟩]Ω+2(∇_Xη)''+2∇_{Jη(X)}Ω.

Thus η and ∇η are the explicit sources of the Nijenhuis Helmholtz equation, while the transverse Bianchi component retains δW₃⁺. For Einstein metrics the third Gray condition is η=0 alone, not η=W₃⁺=0. AAD's local classification, rather than the rough-Laplacian sign by itself, then puts a strict solution in this branch into the Ricci-flat NPT/Tod family. ∫|∇²Ω|²+(3s/4)∫q=4∫|η|²=4[β]²,
where β=iF_A−(s/4)Ω and [β]=2πc₁−(s/4)[Ω]. For s<0 this becomes ∫|∇²Ω|²=3|s|∫q/4+4∫|η|², so it measures rather than eliminates torsion. The transverse Bianchi equation additionally gives the signed pairing

This Step attacked the negative-scalar Goldberg problem (Problem 4) in two ways. It reformulated the problem so that the role of each piece is visible, and it ran exact tests in symmetry-reduced cases, where local existence can actually be decided.

(1) Soldered-instanton formulation. Atiyah–Hitchin–Singer: g is Einstein iff the Levi-Civita connection A+ on Λ+ has self-dual curvature. An almost-Kähler structure is a unit harmonic section σ of Λ+. In the AAD frame the connection is A=(b,Ja,a) with curvature F=dA+½A×A. Its components are exactly AAD's Ricci identities: F1=db−a∧Ja=−R(Ω), F2=d(Ja)+a∧b=−R(φ), F3=da−Ja∧b=−R(Jφ). The second fundamental form α of σ is an L-valued 1-form, L=σ^⊥, and it satisfies three things:
- the AK condition puts α in Ω^{0,1}_J(L), where J is soldered to σ;
- the Einstein condition gives (d_b α)^-=0, three complex equations for two unknowns, so the system is overdetermined;
- harmonicity gives d_b^*α=2η.
So (d^*+d^-)α=(2η,0). This is the ASD deformation operator, and its Bochner formula has Ricci term s/4<0. It reproduces Step-55 identity (7.1) and nothing more. The only information beyond ordinary instanton theory is the type restriction together with the soldering. Every proof or counterexample must use exactly these two features.

The σ-component of the instanton Bianchi identity gives a sourced Maxwell equation for the canonical U(1) connection, d^*F1=j=−η·a+W3+·a. This current is algebraic in (η, W3+, a), and δβ=−j−d^*(a∧Ja). So b is not Yang–Mills; its current is the η- and W3+-weighted Nijenhuis charge. Spirit's remainder ‖β−H‖²=∫q²/16−8π²‖c1^{−,h}‖² was verified. Since Ric<0 on 1-forms, Hodge theory alone gives no spectral control of dξ.

(2) The h-tested Bianchi functional F_h. A02 asked whether its h-tested functional F_h has an intrinsic cancellation. In the J-test (Step-55 eq. 7.5), W3+(e_j,Je_k) stays self-dual, so it meets only the skew (curvature) part of ∇²Ω, and the result is algebraic. In the h-test, W3+(e_j,he_k) lies in Λ+⊗Λ-, i.e. it is trace-free symmetric in (j,k). It therefore pairs with Sym0∇²Ω, which AAD does not determine. It also pairs with the twistor component of ∇h. So no intrinsic cancellation exists at this order. Any cancellation must come from an equation for Sym0∇²Ω, i.e. the next prolongation of AAD (47). This Step moved the closed negative Goldberg problem (Q4) from local zero-germ algebra to global curvature consequences of the forced torsion charge. At a zero the Rayleigh quotient of W^+ on Ω/√2 is exactly the Kähler value s/6, so |W^+|^2>=s^2/24 there. The relative Euler class of T is therefore supported where W^+ is at least Kähler-sized along Ω. Kähler–Einstein metrics sit exactly on the boundary λ_min=s/6, |W^+|^2=s^2/24.

The complete Bianchi-VIII/Fino pair confirms exactly that this localization is sharp. Its eigenvalue gaps w_i+2 and its pinching deficit |W^+|^2-s^2/24 are explicit rational functions, strictly positive and strictly negative respectively at every finite point, and reach equality only at p→1. This turns the explicit control from a mere counter-indication into a structural illustration: the open pinched region supports complete strict AKE geometry, and only compactness plus positive charge forbids it.

The second idea is that the AK form of a Kähler metric is rigid in its own orientation. On a compact Kähler surface, a compatible AK form in the complex orientation is fω_I+Reθ with f constant and θ holomorphic. Constant length forces θ to be parallel, so Ω is Kähler with no exceptions. In the opposite orientation, the commuting pair (I,J) gives an orthogonal splitting into two foliations by I-holomorphic curves, automatically minimal. J is Kähler iff both foliations are totally geodesic, i.e. the metric is locally a product. Corollary 60.2 excludes this case whenever λ_min(W^-_I)>s/6, in particular on reversed ball quotients where W^-_I=0.

- a manifold diffeomorphic to a compact real-hyperbolic quotient carries no AKE structure at all;
- on one diffeomorphic to a compact ball quotient, every AKE structure is the standard Kähler one up to diffeomorphism, scale and sign.
For locally H^2×H^2 metrics every compatible AK structure is Kähler, and Goldberg on those manifolds reduces to Einstein uniqueness. On a minimal general-type surface, Goldberg in the complex orientation reduces to whether every Einstein metric there is Kähler, an open problem LeBrun singles out. This explains structurally why Q4 is hard: any closed counterexample is a non-Kähler Einstein metric, which is itself an unresolved existence question. Such a metric must concentrate Kähler-sized W^+ on the charged set.

There is a real connection to Q1. On a nonminimal general-type surface no KE metric exists. So any Einstein metric that is almost-Kähler for a symplectic form must be strictly AK, and Q1 and Q4 meet exactly in strict AKE metrics on blowups. I also derived a deformation picture at KE: the linear AKE space is Koiso deformations ⊕ ReH^{2,0}, and the H^{2,0} directions are obstructed at second order by Δ|σ|^2. This is consistent with Lemma 60.3 but only a sketch.
