mathematical_discussion:
Step 60 contained a useful curvature organizer for the closed negative Goldberg problem, but this review separated three geometrically different strata that had been partly conflated. For u=Ω/√2 and q=|∇Ω|², the harmonic-form Weitzenböck identity gives r=⟨W⁺u,u⟩=s/6+q/4. Writing W⁺ in the splitting Ru⊕u⊥ with transverse block η and trace-free component W₃⁺ yields the exact identity

|W⁺|²−s²/24=|η|²+|W₃⁺|²+sq/8+3q²/32.

At a torsion zero q=0 this becomes |W⁺|²−s²/24=|η|²+|W₃⁺|². Thus every zero has Rayleigh quotient s/6 and lies where λ_min(W⁺)≤s/6 and |W⁺|²≥s²/24, but those two threshold relations carry different information. Norm equality forces η=W₃⁺=0 and the full Kähler-type operator diag(s/6,−s/12,−s/12). Equality λ_min=s/6 requires η=0 together with the requirement that the complementary eigenvalues are no smaller than s/6; nonzero W₃⁺ can either preserve or violate this depending on its size. In particular nonzero η forces λ_min<s/6, while topology and the Rayleigh identity do not place first-order charged zeros on either equality stratum. The supported top Chern class remains localized in the region λ_min≤s/6, but no quantitative Weyl-energy payment or index restriction follows from that localization alone.

The complete Bianchi-VIII/Fino pair remains an exact control. Its three eigenvalues satisfy λ_min(W⁺)>−2 and |W⁺|²<6 at every finite point for s=−12, with equality approached only at the infinite end where q→0. The Step-60 script is mathematically consistent, but two root counters labeled as open-interval counts include the endpoint p=1; the note's substantive sign conclusions are correct. At the bolt q=32/3, η=W₃⁺=0 and |W⁺|²=2/3, exactly reproducing the general identity. The model therefore shows that the strictly pinched open region supports complete strict AKE geometry; compactness and the nonzero torsion charge are the added global ingredients.

The fixed-metric Kähler results were also clarified. In the complex orientation of a compact Kähler surface, every compatible almost-Kähler form is parallel. Its harmonic decomposition is Ω=fω_I+Re θ with f constant and θ holomorphic; constant |Ω| makes |θ| constant, and a constant-norm holomorphic section of the canonical line bundle is parallel for its Chern/Levi-Civita connection. If θ is nonzero the Ricci form vanishes, so for a non-Ricci-flat metric Ω=±ω_I. This is an established Apostolov–Drăghici result rather than an uncited new observation.

For the opposite orientation, closed complementary forms produce smooth I-invariant involutive plane fields whose leaves are minimal complex curves. They do not automatically produce holomorphic line subbundles of T^{1,0}M. If the orthogonal projector Π were ∂̄_I-holomorphic, self-adjointness and compatibility of the Chern connection would already force Π to be parallel, which is essentially the desired product conclusion rather than a free input. The Tod/AAD local models demonstrate that closed complementary rank-one forms and minimal complex leaves can coexist with a nonparallel splitting. Consequently Baum–Bott or Brunella theory cannot be invoked until transverse holomorphicity is derived from additional equations.

The primary Apostolov–Drăghici survey and Apostolov–Drăghici–Moroianu splitting paper place this opposite-orientation route in its exact representation. If a negative Kähler–Einstein metric h admits a commuting opposite almost-Kähler structure with splitting D₊⊕D₋, then h_t=h|D₊+t h|D₋ is Kähler for I and almost-Kähler for the opposite structure, has unchanged Ricci form, and its Ricci endomorphism has constant eigenvalues λ and λ/t. Conversely, a Kähler surface with two distinct negative constant Ricci eigenvalues gives such a negative Kähler–Einstein metric. The unresolved compact nonproduct alternative already has strong topology: the surface is minimal of general type with ample canonical bundle and even positive signature. Thus the rescaling does not prove splitting in negative curvature; it identifies the precise established form of the remaining problem.

The locally symmetric and fixed-manifold conclusions survive with corrected attribution. The standard real-hyperbolic metric admits no compatible almost-Kähler structure; a complex-hyperbolic metric admits only ±ω_I in its complex orientation and none in the reverse orientation; product H²×H² metrics admit only parallel compatible forms after a factor-preserving finite cover. Combined with Besson–Courtois–Gallot and LeBrun Einstein rigidity, this settles the all-Einstein-metric Goldberg question on manifolds diffeomorphic to compact real- or complex-hyperbolic quotients. These are complete classwise consequences, but the difficult center of closed Goldberg remains the charged torsion-zero geometry, not an expanding catalogue of rigid backgrounds.

A02's message #849 substantially sharpened that center. Its exact soldered equation identifies the primitive (1,1) part of d_bα with Ric″, so Einstein AKE torsion satisfies an overdetermined elliptic first-order equation. At a nondegenerate zero the permitted first jet is f(z)=cz+B bar(z), B=S+A with S complex symmetric and A antisymmetric. Independent TTCS verification established

det_R Df=|c|⁴−|c|²(||S||²−||A||²)+|det B|².

Writing t=|c|², d=||S||²−||A||² and ρ=|det B|, negative index occurs exactly when d>2ρ and t lies strictly between (d±√(d²−4ρ²))/2. Pure c, pure A and nondegenerate pure S modes all have positive index; negative index requires interaction between c and a sufficiently large symmetric mode. The same curvature-visible c and A can support either sign as S varies, so the unseen symmetric derivative is the decisive local degree of freedom. In particular η=0, equivalently c=0 in these coordinates, forces positive index at a nondegenerate zero, but that is compatible with the globally positive total charge and gives no contradiction.

A02's canonical-connection computation also removes a tempting global route. Its smooth c₂(E) density is positive on the complete strict pair, increasing from 6/(4π²) at the bolt to 42/(4π²) at infinity, and the difference from the Levi-Civita representative is exactly the AAD balance transgression. Smooth Chern–Weil representatives therefore do not detect signed local torsion indices. Any successful use of c₂(E) must depend on the torsion section itself, an off-zero opposite structure, or a localized Thom/Mathai–Quillen mechanism.

The highest-value next mathematics is consequently the first nonlinear compatibility at a torsion zero, with the symmetric mode retained. The intrinsic target is the U(2)-equivariant quadratic relation on the first-jet space (c,A,S) produced by Hess q=2⟨∇T,∇T⟩, Hess κ=3⟨∇T,∇T⟩, differentiated Einstein/AAD Bianchi equations, and the remaining curvature variables. It must be tested on the pure c, pure A, pure S and mixed negative-index sectors, with exact Kähler and Ricci-flat Gibbons–Hawking finite-order zeros as controls. A02 is computing the same stage in Darboux metric variables; an independent intrinsic reduction would provide meaningful cross-representation verification. Compatibility through one order would not construct a germ, while a genuine incompatibility on every charge-carrying sector could materially advance closed Goldberg. Problems 1–3, the α≤1 law, certified sub-four construction, Burns insertion theorem, and O10/O11 remain active and unchanged.

mathematical_discussion:
This Step moved the closed negative Goldberg problem (Q4) from an open-ended principal zero-germ family to a proved nonlinear restriction at torsion zeros.

Let (M,g,Ω) be Einstein almost-Kähler, with u=Ω/√2 and q=|∇Ω|². Write W⁺ as the block matrix [[r,η^T],[η,−r/2 I+V]] in Ru⊕u^⊥. Here W⁺ is an endomorphism with Kähler spectrum (s/6,−s/12,−s/12), η is the off-diagonal endomorphism vector, and trV² is a Frobenius square.

Two standard identities combine:
- the harmonic-form Weitzenböck identity q=4⟨W⁺u,u⟩−2s/3;
- Derdziński's Einstein identity ∇*∇W⁺=−(s/2)W⁺+6W⁺²−2tr(W⁺²)Id.
Taking ∇*∇ of the first at a point where ∇Ω=0 gives Theorem 62.A:
|∇²Ω|²=4trV²−12|η|².
All λ-dependent terms cancel. The identity is the pointwise trace of Hess q=2⟨∇T,∇T⟩. Its trace-free part is absorbed by the free trace-free part of ∇²W⁺. That is the structural answer Spirit asked for: S is not a free curvature-invisible mode, because the scalar trace fixes it against A and c.

A TTCS verifier derived the exact coframe dictionary from the AAD Ricci identities da=−R(ψ), d(Ja)=−R(φ). For the first jet f=cz+(S+A)z̄:
- |η|²=4|c|² and trV²=4‖A‖²;
- S contributes nothing to W⁺(p);
- |∇²Ω|²=4(4|c|²+2‖A‖²+2‖S‖²).
Theorem 62.A is therefore exactly the real quadric cone ‖A‖²=8|c|²+‖S‖² inside the 10-dimensional admissible linear first-jet space L=2(c)+2(A)+6(S).

A02's determinant det_R Df=|c|⁴−|c|²(‖S‖²−‖A‖²)+|det B|² was checked exactly. On the cone it becomes 9|c|⁴+|det B|². Since |det S|≤‖S‖²/2 and |a|²=4|c|²+‖S‖²/2, one gets |det B|≥4|c|², so det≥25|c|⁴. Every nondegenerate torsion zero of an Einstein AK four-manifold therefore has index +1. Further consequences:
- pure c, pure S and pure A jets are excluded;
- any nonzero first jet forces W₃⁺≠0 and |W⁺|²−s²/24=|∇²Ω|²/4+5|η|²>0;
- W₃⁺(p)=0 forces ∇²Ω(p)=0;
- degenerate order-one zeros are exactly c=0, S with equal singular values, det S=−a². Ricci-flat Gibbons–Hawking zeros are of this type.

This removes the negative-index mechanism A02 found in the linear algebra. It does not contradict the forced total charge 5χ+6τ>0; positive nondegenerate zeros are what topology asks for. If all zeros are nondegenerate there are exactly 5χ+6τ of them.

The global consequence proposed by the TTCS generator sharpens the problem. Each torsion zero is a strict minimum of q. Under nondegeneracy and isolated critical points, Poincaré–Hopf for ∇q gives total index −2(2χ+3τ)<0 on the strict region. A closed counterexample therefore needs at least 2(2χ+3τ) odd-index strict critical points, or negative-Euler critical surfaces like the genus-g bolt maximum of the complete Bianchi-VIII pair. A Morse-parity theorem for Hess q at strict critical points would close this case; this is a new global target. The generator also gave an unverified second-order-zero identity |∇³Ω|²=4ΣtrV_i²−24Σ|η_i|², again λ-independent.

The decisive judgment is now sharper. Every identity found at zeros so far is λ-blind, and the Ricci-flat GH controls survive them. A sign-of-λ obstruction must therefore come at subleading higher order, or globally. Conversely, an actual negative-λ analytic germ with an isolated cone zero would show that local zero exclusion cannot close Goldberg.

An SU(2) nut is the natural construction test. There S=0, ‖A‖²=8|c|² and det=25|c|⁴. A triaxial cohomogeneity-one AKE ODE with three-direction x_i(t) is accessible to the Step-57 metric-only class-A machinery with n=(1,1,1). At T² or U(2) fixed points all invariant first jets vanish.

Numerical continuation in an independent jet gauge supports, but does not prove, that the cone is the complete obstruction:
- D=4 and D=5 at λ=−1: on-cone jets converge;
- D=6: generic cone jets converge at λ=−1 and λ=0;
- some D=6 starts (A+S, GH) stalled at the initial t=0 Kähler solve or at t=0.2, which reads as LM conditioning, not obstruction.
The opposite-orientation projector route remains a restricted complementary class. Its new global information would be control of the mixed class x²−y². Q1–Q3, α≤1, the certified <3.9961512 cell, Burns insertion and O10/O11 remain unchanged.

mathematical_discussion:
This Step converted the Step-62 torsion-zero cone into two complementary advances for the closed negative-scalar Goldberg problem. First, it produced a global assembly theorem for positive-dimensional zero sets. Second, it subjected the proposed diagonal SU(2)-nut realization of an isolated cone zero to exact symmetry-reduced equations and found a genuine rigidity mechanism rather than a numerical failure.

For an Einstein almost-Kähler four-manifold, let T=∇Ω. The Step-62 first-jet cone and determinant formula imply that whenever a smooth surface C lies in {T=0}, tangential vanishing makes DT singular and hence forces c=0. At a point where DT is nonzero, DT is complex-antilinear of complex rank one, its kernel is the J-complex tangent line TC, η=0, and W3+ is nonzero. Since W3+ is a section of K_J^{-2}, its nowhere-zero restriction would trivialize K_J^{-2}|C. The actual canonical Chern form supplies incompatible global information: on C, a=0 and R(Ω)=(s/4)Ω, so 2π c1(M,J)[C]=(s/4)Area(C). Therefore, for s≠0, no compact smooth embedded surface contained in the torsion-zero set can have DT everywhere nonzero. This is a direct connection between the nonlinear zero cone, actual canonical curvature, and topology; it uses neither a surrounding holomorphic foliation nor a scalar energy estimate.

The same argument sharpens the exceptional-point problem. If a compact smooth zero surface has a dense rank-two locus, then TC is J-invariant by continuity, η=0 everywhere on C, and W3+ vanishes exactly where DT=0. Its degree is

deg(K_J^{-2}|C)=s Area(C)/(4π)=2(χ(C)+C·C).

For s<0 this degree is negative. If the exceptional zeros are isolated, their signed windings must sum negatively, so at least one must have negative winding. No contradiction follows yet because W3+ is a smooth section and no tangential holomorphic equation has been proved. The mathematically sharp missing information is now whether the differentiated Einstein–AAD equations permit a negative tangential winding of W3+ at a point where T=DT=0 on a J-complex zero surface. This is more specific than another scalar balance or unconstrained degree ladder.

This Step replaced the numerically observed universal multiplier with an exact structural theory, and it pushed a nondegenerate negative-Einstein torsion zero through Ricci degree 8.

Flat compatibility. In Darboux gauge (fixed ω, g=e^H with H anti-J symmetric) the AKE system is overdetermined by exactly one scalar equation. Write P(E)=J_ia J_jb ∂a∂b E_ij − ½Δ trE, which is −2 divdiv E^{anti-J} modulo the contracted Bianchi rows. The identity P(δRic h)≡0 for anti-J h has a one-line proof: J^T h J=−h and tr h=0. Every excess condition at every order is therefore a Taylor coefficient of one scalar equation P_g(E_g)=Γ(g), where Γ is at least quadratic. At d=2 its value is the Step-62 cone, i.e. the zero value of the Δq identity.

Representation theory. Under U(2)=SU(2)_L×U(1)_R, only the radial functional Δ^{m/2}(0) on even-degree scalars is invariant, and there is none at odd degree. A universal surviving row must therefore be ℓ_d=Δ^{(d−2)/2}P(E_d)(0), the spherical-mean moment of the scalar compatibility. The earlier cosine of 0.976 was exactly the Bianchi component of the integer representative. So Φ6=F0+F1λ+F2λ² is the minimal radial fourth moment of one natural invariant. Its sign changes on the cone are a property of that invariant, not of the numerical pipeline. This answers A02's request that ℓ be identified.

Once torsion is present, the radial moment at order ≥6 is protected from the newest jet and must be paid by lower data; at E6 this produces the positive-definite 12-dimensional H4·H4 block and A02's sign condition. This structural fact needs an explanation through the nonlinear identity: plausibly the linearization of Γ at a torsion jet lands its radial part in the image of L^T. Such an explanation could predict whether a definite block, and hence an obstruction, reappears at some even order.

This is the first finite real jet of a negative-Einstein AKE germ with a nondegenerate index-+1 torsion zero through Ricci degree 8. The pattern is now: one radial scalar per even order; the top channel never pays it; at E6 it is paid by a definite lower block (sign condition); at E8, at this point, it is paid by an indefinite or surjective lower structure with no fold. mathematical_discussion:
This Step turned the Step-68/69 finite tables for the Darboux AKE prolongation into all-degree linear theorems. The central idea was to pass from the real Darboux engine to a complex flat model in which the overdetermined structure can be seen directly. Write an anti-J metric variation on flat C^2 as h = mu_ab dz_a dz_b + nu_ab dzbar_a dzbar_b, with mu = conj(nu) symmetric. The flat linearized Ricci operator (tr h = 0) splits into two parts. The J-anti-invariant part is E1_ab = dbar_a D_b + dbar_b D_a - 2 Box nu_ab, with D_b = d_c nu_cb and Box = d_c dbar_c. The J-invariant part is E2_ab = d_a d_c nu_cb + dbar_b dbar_c mu_ca. The principal torsion, dbar of the Beltrami differential, is v_a = dbar_1 nu_a2 - dbar_2 nu_a1. This model reproduces the Darboux-engine counts exactly: dim ker 127 and 244, torsion rank 22 and 34 at d=4,6.

(1) Flat half-twistor identity, pointwise and exact. The trace-free holomorphic derivative of v is a combination of E1 alone: d_{z1}v_2 = -E1_22/2, d_{z2}v_1 = E1_11/2, and d_{z1}v_1 - d_{z2}v_2 = -E1_12. This is the flat principal form of A02's 75.H(a). Whenever Ric''=0 we get d_{z_b}v_a = delta_ab phi. Comparing mixed derivatives forces phi = h(zbar), so v = z h(zbar) + g(zbar). Containment in the half-twistor space HT_n therefore holds in every degree.

(2) Surjectivity in every degree, by explicit kernel elements.
- g-part: every antiholomorphic symmetric nu(w) lies in ker L, since D=0, Box nu=0 and dbar mu=0. Its torsion is the w-curl. By the polynomial Poincaré lemma, whose kernel consists of the Hessians dbar dbar phi, this curl is onto all antiholomorphic vector polynomials of degree n+1.
- h-part: for h = w1^n take nu11 = -w1^{n-1} w2 (w1 z1 + (n/2) w2 z2), nu12 = -w1^n w2 z2, nu22 = 0. A hand check gives E1 = E2 = 0 and v = z w1^n. The realized set of h is a complex U(2)-invariant subspace containing w1^n, because unitary pullback sends h to det(Ubar) h(Ubar w). It is therefore all of Sym^n.
- Hence T(ker L_n) = HT_n, of real dimension 6n+10, for every n >= 0.

(3) Torsion-free kernel. If v=0, then nu = dbar dbar phi with phi complex, determined modulo A(z) + w.B(z). E1 vanishes identically and E2_ab = d_a dbar_b Box (2 Re phi). The kernel condition is therefore that Box Re phi be pluriharmonic, while Im phi (Hamiltonian gauge) is free. Counting with N = n+4 gives C(n+7,3) + (n+5)^2 + 2(n+3) - (6N+2). Adding 6n+10 yields dim ker L_n = C(n+7,3) + (n+5)^2 + 2n - 10 = 50, 84, 127, 180, 244, 320, 409, ... This matches every value computed earlier.

(4) Polynomial exactness in every degree. SymPy verifies the identity C(n+7,3) + (n+5)^2 + 2n - 10 = 6C(n+5,3) - 10C(n+3,3) + 4C(n+2,3) + C(n+1,3). Consequently dim coker L_n = 4C(n+2,3) + C(n+1,3): exactly the number of contracted-Bianchi rows (degree n-1) plus P rows (degree n-2). Both families annihilate the image (the flat Bianchi identity and P∘δRic=0). They are independent because their combined operator Θ is surjective. By Fischer duality this is equivalent to injectivity of multiplication by the 10x5 symbol matrix, which has rank 5 at xi=e1: the matrices e1e1-δ/2, sym(e_k e1) and e2e2-δ/2 are independent. Therefore every polynomial compatibility of the flat Darboux AKE system is generated by Bianchi and the single scalar operator P, in every degree. This is the graded exactness theorem that Spirit #78 named as the missing bridge, and it replaces the finite cokernel table through d=8.

(5) Newest-jet channel, all degrees. The channel is M_d = P(B(H2,k) - λk) on ker L_{d-2}.
- λk contributes nothing: for k in ker L, P(k) ∝ δs(k) = 0.
- Hamiltonian-gauge k contribute zero, because the pullback is exact and E_base = O(|x|^d).
- Structural argument: for every AK metric, q = 2<W+Ω,Ω> - 2s/3 holds. Hence (Δq - RHS_65) is a universal expression in the differential ideal of E = Ric - λg, involving ∇^{≤2}E only. By weight counting its ∇²E coefficient uses only g and Ω.
- U(2) invariance reduces that principal part, modulo Bianchi, to the span of Δ trE and JJ∂∂E. The only element annihilating Im L is P. The principal part is therefore c·P with a universal constant c.
- Degree counting shows that the k-variation of all other E-terms vanishes at degree n. The k-variation of Δq - RHS at degree n is the polarization at f1 of the homogeneous Step-65 identity in the direction v = T(k). It depends on k only through v, since δη and δW3+ are first derivatives of v and W1+ is quadratic in torsion.

- For n >= 3 the four types (0,n), (1,n-1) and their conjugates are distinct, so the real part is injective.
- When B ≠ 0, g makes Q0 onto (0,n). When det B ≠ 0, h ↦ Q1 is injective. The rank is therefore exactly 4(n+1): 20, 28, 36 at n=4,6,8.
- If B has rank one the rank is 4n+2. At the Kähler first jet it is 0. At n=2 the self-conjugate type (1,1) gives 10.
- New cone lemma: |det B| >= |a|^2 - |det S| >= (||A||^2 - ||S||^2)/2 = 4|c|^2. This uses |det S| <= ||S||^2/2 and det(S+A) = det S + a^2. So every nondegenerate cone jet has invertible B. It also re-derives det Df = 9|c|^4 + |det B|^2 >= 25|c|^4.

This identifies precisely what lower-order data must pay at each order. The deeper reformulation now visible: because P is the only compatibility and its nonlinear form is the Δq defect, the entire formal AKE problem at a torsion zero becomes a torsion-only recursion. At each even order, sum over m1+m2 = n+2 of R(f_m1, f_m2), plus scalar-curvature terms, must vanish in the middle bidegrees. The newest pairing (f1, f_{n+1}) can absorb only the extreme bidegrees. A formal-existence theorem would need surjectivity of these lower pairings onto the middle bidegrees, not another definite block.

Globally, closed negative Goldberg remains open. The local theory is now essentially linear-algebraically complete; the open local issue is the nonlinear middle-bidegree solvability across the tower. The global information still has to come from the canonical ASD flux and Weyl fluctuation budget identified in Step 69, or from compact transport. The witness, from the polished gen5 λ=-5 point, has been independently re-evaluated by A02 (#863), who obtained the same unreduced residuals, E0 2.7e-15 through E8 9.8e-7.

The outcome has two sides.

(1) The scalar compatibility source is a coupled torsion–curvature object. On the tangent Tan of the lower solution variety {E2..E_{K-2}=0}, the scalar map dP_K(E_K) was restricted to several subspaces:
- lower jets frozen (the newest channel);
- lower jets moved only by Hamiltonian gauge;
- lower jets moved with their principal torsion fixed, i.e. gauge plus the physical curvature fibre.
The ranks on these three subspaces are 20/20/34 out of 35 at K=6, on two backgrounds (gen5 λ=-5 and gen2 λ=0), and 28/28/69 out of 84 at K=8. The curvature fibre therefore supplies 14 of the 15 rows the newest channel misses at K=6, and 41 of 56 at K=8. Gauge adds nothing, as it must.

Fixing all odd coordinate Nijenhuis Taylor coefficients N3..N_{K-1} removes every lower-jet direction: the residual fibre equals the top torsion-free flat kernel (210 at K=6 and 363 at K=8), and dR vanishes on it. So torsion Taylor data are complete coordinates on Tan, but they are not freely prescribed half-twistors. Lower W^-–type curvature data change the higher torsion coefficients through the Einstein equation. The Step-70 picture of a bilinear torsion-only recursion with free homogeneous f_m is therefore wrong as stated. The correct picture is a coupled recursion in which the curvature freedom absorbs most of the non-invariant compatibilities. This also makes a generic local formal obstruction at nondegenerate index-+1 zeros look increasingly unlikely; together with the order-8 submersion confirmed by both sessions, local exclusion of nondegenerate zeros appears dead.

(2) The U(2)-invariant radial compatibility ℓ_K (Δ^{(K-2)/2} at 0) is numerically torsion-only. On full Tan it is 7.25, 4.97 and 0.93, and it is 0.77 when only H6 moves.
My explanation is conjectural: the Δq identity contains only torsion, W^+ and s, never W^-. If coordinate-moment corrections drop out, the invariant hierarchy is a functional of torsion jets alone.
This would sharpen the local–global interface for closed negative Goldberg. W^- data can absorb all local non-invariant obstruction. A zero-local condition that could carry global meaning must lie in the invariant radial hierarchy, and that hierarchy sees only torsion. The same is true of the global inputs: the charge 5χ+6τ of the torsion section, the AAD torsion/W3+ balance, and the canonical ASD flux q·ω̂. This is a reason to formulate the global route entirely through torsion-built invariants and W^+, not through W^-. R=P+S/4=8π^2(A+k)+σ/3+2w.

The proposed matching construction is now supported by primary source geometry. The strongest advance in this Step is to replace the canonical-cycle-only viewpoint by the closed semipositive two-form

\[\beta=\gamma-\frac{s}{4}\omega,\qquad [\beta]=2\pi c_1(J)-\frac{s}{4}[\omega].\]

For a closed negative Einstein almost-Kähler four-manifold, Step 77 gives \(\gamma(P)=s/4+|a_{P^\perp}|^2\) on every \(J\)-complex plane, hence \(\beta(P)=|a_{P^\perp}|^2\ge0\). Since \(d\gamma=d\omega=0\) and \(s\) is constant, \(\beta\) is closed. Thus every actual \(J\)-holomorphic current \(C\) satisfies \(\beta(C)\ge0\), and \(\omega+t\beta\) tames the same \(J\) for every \(t\ge0\). This converts the Einstein canonical-connection curvature into a functional on the entire Taubes-effective cone, rather than one selected canonical current.

Primary-source reading fixes the available curve supply. LeBrun 2005 already proves the canonical-connection formula and the two-sided curvature inequality on every \(J\)-holomorphic curve; his Corollary 3.5 produces a fixed-\(J\) current in every class \(a\) for which \(c_1+2a\) is a nonzero Seiberg-Witten basic class when \(b^+>1\), and his Theorem B explicitly applies this to the minimal pullback \(K_0\) and all exceptional classes on a blowup. Chen–Zhang Theorem A.4 independently gives an actual current in every exceptional class for every tame \(J\) outside the rational exception, and Proposition A.5 treats positive exceptional combinations. Taubes's maximal-pairing theorem and the Li–Liu formulation give an equivalent symplectic-ray interpretation: applying the signed blowup basic classes to \(\omega+t\beta\) and sending \(t\to\infty\) forces the corresponding \(\beta\)-periods to be nonnegative.

Consequently, in the \(b^+>1\) blowup setting with verified decomposition \(K=K_0+\sum_{i=1}^rE_i\), actual signed-basic-class supply gives \(\beta(K_0)\ge0\), while
\[\beta(E_i)=2\pi+\frac{|s|}{4}\omega(E_i).\]

\[2\pi\beta(K)=T_{\rm AK}-\int|\eta|_{62}^2,\]
one obtains the strengthened quantitative law
\[T_{\rm AK}-\int|\eta|_{62}^2\ge4\pi^2r+\frac{\pi|s|}{2}\sum_i\omega(E_i).\]
This is substantially stronger, under its matching field and curve supply, than the earlier \(T_{\rm AK}\ge2\pi^2k\) consequence. It implies in particular
\[T_{\rm AK}\ge4\pi^2r+\frac{\pi|s|}{2}\sum_i\omega(E_i),\]
and, using \(s^2V=32\pi^2(K_0^2-r)+16T_{\rm AK}\),
\[s^2V\ge32\pi^2K_0^2+32\pi^2r+8\pi|s|\sum_i\omega(E_i).\]
The same mechanism applies to every Taubes-effective class, so \([\beta]\) lies in the dual cone of the actual basic-class current supply. It does not invalidate every argument using local identities and integration by parts. The most valuable continuation is therefore to combine the new effective-cone information with the full Bianchi equations while preserving their divergence current.

This Step carried Spirit #88's two suggestions for closed negative Goldberg through to exact general identities, with model checks and one falsification. It also turned an implicit limitation of every regularized-identity route into a precise statement.

First, the normalized-section picture is exact, and E1 simplifies in general. Because K is antilinear, K(∂r)=K(Y)+η̄K(α), so E1 collapses to ∂_Dη=vα+iK(Y). Take σ_f=f/√h, α̂=α/√h (with |α̂|²<1/2) and Ỹ=Y/h. Then the logarithmic drift is ∂log h=4(Ỹ+σ_ηα̂). In the σ-form of E1/E2, every drift term is either Ỹ, which is the L²-controlled square in (80.S), or a σσα̂ product with α̂ bounded. The weighted Kodaira currents are the ordinary currents of σ, since j_σ=j_f/h. In the weighted W⁺ Bochner identity, the weight term 3r/8·|dq|²/h² has a favourable sign near zeros. After σ-normalization the residual obstruction is the quartic product |σ|²|Ỹ+σ_ηα̂|², with net coefficient −1/2 for σ_v and no matching square for σ_η. Together with the free jets ∂̄σ_v and S, this is a genuine loss of coercivity, not an artifact of splitting the current.

Second, a structural principle (Proposition 81.T). At any fixed ε, every identity built from currents w(q,r,ε)·P(fields, first derivatives) with bounded weights also holds on the complete Bianchi-VIII model: the fluxes vanish and the densities are integrable there. Hence no fixed-ε pointwise certificate Φ≥κq/h can exist, and an SDP multiplier search at fixed ε is pointless. The only compactness-sensitive density is the field-free weight ε/h. On a closed manifold ∫ε/h→Vol(Z)=0, while on the model it diverges like ε^{-2/3}. The sharp target is therefore a certificate Φ_ε≥κq/h−Cε/h−(zero-localized terms with vanishing limits). The model does not exclude such a certificate, and one would prove Goldberg. At ε=0 this is a uniform normalized superharmonicity of log q away from zeros. The model satisfies −Δlog q≥|s|/2 at every sampled point, whereas near any finite-order zero Δlog q≈4m/ρ²>0. The problem thus becomes a quantitative logarithmic mass balance. On one side is the positive mass carried near the forced torsion zeros, whose number is set by c₂(E)=5χ+6τ. On the other is the negative bulk mass, proportional to V with s²V=32π²c₁²+16T_AK. Both are topological at the curvature scale. This is the most promising new global formulation for Goldberg, and a lower bound on the bulk −Δlog q together with an upper bound on the near-zero positive mass would close the problem.

Third, the dd^c analysis. In general Θ_u=dd^cu splits into a Levi-Civita Levi form plus a Nijenhuis part √2Re(α(∇u)ψ), which follows from α∧ι_Xψ=α(X)ψ. The (1,1) part of β is rank one: it vanishes on the torsion line ℓ_α and equals q/4 on the complementary J-line. Closedness of β gives, for every u, ∫⟨Θ_u⁻,γ⁻⟩=∫⟨du,2X−dq/8⟩. For u=log h this yields a new regularized identity for the primitive anisotropy of the Levi form: ∫(q/8)[L(ℓ_α^⊥)−L(ℓ_α)]=∫(2q|η|²−4|Y|²)/h. Scalar pairing with γ adds no surface canonical-degree information beyond Step 63, because β|_C=0 on torsion-zero J-surfaces. Any new information must come from the anisotropic part.

Fourth, the torsion first jet. D''α is pure trace in general, ∝η̄, with |D_Z̄α|²=|η|²/2 and D_Z̄α parallel to α along ℓ_α. On the model the Levi form satisfies L_{log q}(ℓ_α)≡s/2=2γ(ℓ_α) to 14 digits, a Poincaré–Lelong-type law. A leading-order test at nondegenerate zeros, using Step-62 cone jets, gives Λ<0 in 6.3% of samples. The law is therefore model-specific and cannot serve as a general psh mechanism; this falsification prevents a false lead.

Assessment. The Goldberg line now has a precise algebraic and global target rather than an open-ended identity search. Its central difficulty is quantitative control of log-mass near the forced zeros against bulk superharmonicity. Problems 1–3 remain parallel open branches: the certified sub-four smooth cells, the exact orbifold law, and the unresolved smooth tariff and attainment problems.

mathematical_discussion:
This Step turned the Step-82 idea 82.K into a moduli-space framework for closed negative Goldberg (Q4). The same framework also bears on Einstein existence on nonminimal general-type surfaces (Q1).

The unifying object is the Weyl deficit of an Einstein metric, D(g)=∫(s²/24−|W⁺|²). Gauss–Bonnet and the signature formula give D=Ŝ²/16−2π²(2χ+3τ), so D is an affine function of the normalized Einstein–Hilbert action Ŝ²=s²Vol. For Kähler metrics D=0. For almost-Kähler Einstein (AKE) metrics the Step-77 AAD balance gives D=T_AK≥0, with equality iff the metric is Kähler. Closed negative Goldberg is therefore exactly the statement that no AKE metric has D>0.

Two independent mechanisms then constrain D.

The first is moduli constancy. Einstein metrics are the critical points of Ŝ, and Koiso's premoduli is a real-analytic subset of a finite-dimensional analytic submanifold, locally arc-connected. Hence Ŝ is locally constant on Einstein metrics. It is therefore constant on connected subsets of the moduli space and takes finitely many values on compact subsets of the smooth moduli. The Schwahn–Semmelmann survey (Thm 3.9, item 'S locally constant on E', line ~390) states this as known, so 83.1 is standard. Its consequences:
- 83.2(a): an AKE metric in a Kähler–Einstein component is Kähler.
- 83.2(b): in reversed orientation T_AK=12π²τ is forced.
- A strict AKE metric lives in a component with constant D>0 that contains no KE metric.

The second mechanism, which I judge the genuinely substantive one, is measure transfer through noncollapsed degeneration. Under bounded diameter and noncollapsing, volume converges and the concentrated W⁺ energy m≥0 enters as D(V)=lim D(g_n)+m. No bubble energy identity is needed. For AKE sequences, two facts combine:
- T_AK is lower semicontinuous with concentrated defect m_T≥0.
- D=T_AK holds on both the smooth metrics and the orbifold limit.
This gives m+m_T=0, so neither self-dual Weyl energy nor torsion energy can concentrate. Every bubble (all tree levels and necks are inside m) is Ricci-flat with W⁺=0, and the rescaled almost-Kähler forms converge to parallel forms by the Weitzenböck identity |∇ω|²=2W⁺(ω,ω). Degenerating AKE families thus produce AKE orbifolds with the same T_AK and orientation-matched Ricci-flat Kähler bubbles; torsion cannot hide in bubbles energetically. This is a rigidity mechanism not available for general Einstein sequences.

The small-torsion consequence is a clean alternative for strict AKE sequences with T_AK→0:
- they leave every compact subset of the smooth moduli;
- if noncollapsed with bounded diameter, they converge to a singular KE orbifold with Kähler bubbles, approaching from larger normalized volume;

This connects the Goldberg gap to the structure of the compactified Einstein moduli: Anderson's subanalyticity expectation as quoted by Ozuch, and Ozuch's gluing-perturbation description, whose obstruction-projection analyticity is unknown for trees. This is a sufficient condition, not an exact reduction.

For Q1, LeBrun 2001 Prop. 4.2 / Thm 4.3 gives ∫|Ric|²≥8π²(A+k) for every metric on X#k CP2bar, all b⁺. For Einstein metrics this is Ŝ²≥32π²(A+k), hence D(g)≥4π²k. Every noncollapsed bounded-diameter Einstein degeneration limit V then has D(V)≥4π²k+m. So no Einstein degeneration on a nonminimal general-type surface lands on an orbifold that is Kähler in the inherited orientation, whatever ALE trees occur. Inherited-orientation AKE endpoints need T_AK(V)≥4π²k. Natural Kähler-orbifold desingularization routes are thus excluded in the open range 1≤k<A/3, while non-Kähler bulks and opposite-orientation KE bulks remain.

Judgment. These results do not prove Goldberg or Q1 existence. They organize where counterexamples or constructions must live, and they identify two sharp open structural questions:
- finiteness of Einstein components near KE orbifolds;
- small-torsion collapse or diameter divergence.
The orbifold Goldberg problem appears as the natural closure of the smooth one. Torsion-zero bookkeeping (c₂(E)=5χ+6τ split between V and the Kähler bubbles) is an unexplored link to the Steps 60–65 index results. Problems 2–3 are untouched this Step.

mathematical_discussion:
Step 83 converted the almost-Kähler Einstein identity D=T_AK into a degeneration theorem: self-dual Weyl concentration enters the bulk deficit with the opposite sign from concentrated torsion, forcing both concentration defects to vanish. This Step asked what this actually makes possible near a one-level Kähler–Einstein A1 orbifold degeneration. The answer is more precise than either a global compactified-moduli conjecture or another scalar torsion identity.

The no-concentration mechanism is sound. After extending the bounded constant-length harmonic form across the orbifold point and applying orbifold Stokes, one has lim D(g_n)=D(V)-m_W and lim T_AK(g_n)=T_AK(V)+m_T. Since D=T_AK on both the smooth pairs and the orbifold pair, m_W+m_T=0, hence m_W=m_T=0. In the one-level A1 case the bubble is therefore Eguchi–Hanson in the orientation for which W⁺=0, and its limiting self-dual form is parallel. What this establishes is absence of any positive amount of unnormalized W⁺ or torsion energy in shrinking regions. It does not control torsion divided by its vanishing total norm, the direction of normalized torsion, or the relation between the parallel form on the ALE bubble and the value of the orbifold form in a common asymptotic frame. A slowly rotating direction on a logarithmically long neck can have vanishing L⁴ derivative energy. A weighted neck theorem is therefore indispensable for direction matching. Spirit #99 also corrects the proposed zero-count route: a Ricci-flat Kähler ALE bubble has zero torsion but carries relative Euler-form charge; Eguchi–Hanson contributes 3/2 through curvature and interface transgression. Thus primary Euler charge cannot contradict bubble Kählerness, and the independent object is the matched normalized direction, not the scalar charge.

The correct local object is the coupled pair (g,ω). In Bianchi gauge, with Ric(g)=Eg and E<0 fixed, define the AKE map by the gauged Einstein equation together with dω=0, the anti-self-dual projection P⁻_gω=0, and |ω|²_g=2. At a Kähler–Einstein pair its linearization is
L(h,β)=(½Δ_E h, dβ, β⁻−½ dot-star_h(ω), 2⟨β,ω⟩−tr h).
The trace and divergence equations put h in the TT Einstein kernel. Nagy’s 2026 result identifies that kernel with J-anti-invariant, divergence-free Kodaira–Spencer tensors satisfying bar-partial h=0; the J-invariant Einstein kernel vanishes for E<0. The algebraic AKE equations then leave β as a primitive self-dual harmonic form. Consequently the formal coupled kernel, modulo simultaneous diffeomorphisms and scaling, splits into metric Kodaira–Spencer directions (h,0) and independent form rotations (0,β), with β in the real part of H^{2,0}. The first summand satisfies the linearized Kähler equation but need not integrate to an actual complex or Einstein family. The second is genuinely nonintegrable at first order because its torsion variation is ∇β, and a nonzero parallel holomorphic two-form is incompatible with negative Ricci curvature. This explains why the energy T_AK begins too high in order to give linear coercivity.

Nagy’s second-order identity h₂⁺=h₁² supplies a deeper bridge: in the volume-normalized gauge, the fixed Kähler form remains algebraically compatible with the Einstein metric through second order. Thus a non-Kähler entrance may be invisible at first order and can first appear through a higher Maurer–Cartan/Kodaira–Spencer obstruction. Pure form rotation is more constrained: expanding the constant-length equation gives a quartic variation proportional to the nonconstant part of |β|², and a nonzero holomorphic two-form cannot have constant nonzero norm on a negative Kähler–Einstein surface. A clean proof of this pure-form exclusion is reachable, but mixed metric/form directions and higher-order entrances still require the finite-dimensional reduced system.

Eguchi–Hanson contributes a completely different pair of sectors. Its L² Einstein kernel is three-dimensional, generated by scale and framed hyperkähler-direction variations, with asymptotic tensors o_k=−r⁻⁴θ₁⁻∘θ_k⁺+O(r⁻⁸). Its bounded self-dual harmonic forms are the three parallel hyperkähler forms; fixed-length rotations give two bounded, nondecaying directions. There is no decaying self-dual harmonic form, since W⁺=s=0 reduces the self-dual Weitzenböck equation to the rough Laplacian and decay forces vanishing. Hence the isolated core supplies no localized strict-AKE form mode. Every core form rotation has a constant asymptotic trace that must match exterior harmonic or Kähler data. The metric modes can be paired locally with hyperkähler-form variations and are torsion-free, although global periods and matching equations determine which combinations survive.

At the Kähler–Einstein orbifold point, the self-dual curvature operator is rank one: R⁺=E I⊗I for I=ω/√2. Ozuch’s leading Eguchi–Hanson obstruction therefore controls the component of the ALE parameter toward I, while the two transverse directions are the smoothing/hyperkähler directions. This does not by itself prove exact orthogonality or local rigidity; parameter-derivative bounds and higher matching terms are still needed. It does, however, show that the core rotation toward the Kähler line is an Einstein-normal variable with a nonzero leading coefficient, whereas the transverse core variables are Kähler smoothing data rather than a strict-AKE entrance.

The resulting research architecture is a three-region weighted pair analysis. Split off every formal center: orbifold Einstein Jacobi fields, exterior primitive harmonic forms, the three Eguchi–Hanson metric modes, constant cone tensors, and the two fixed-length parallel-form rotations. Seek a uniform estimate of the form ||x_perp||≤C(||L_εx_perp||+matching traces+model projections). Failure would produce an exterior kernel, a cone-neck homogeneous mode, or an Eguchi–Hanson kernel; the extracted moments should eliminate each. This estimate reduces the problem to a finite map containing both the Einstein obstruction and the harmonic constant-length equation. A local curve-selection or action-gradient inequality for this particular reduced map would then combine with action constancy and Step 83 to eliminate strict AKE zeros approaching the Kähler endpoint. Such regularity is one possible closure mechanism, not an assumption about the entire compactified Einstein moduli and not yet established. A direct normal coercive estimate could replace it.

This advances closed Goldberg by identifying exactly where compact information must enter: matched pair directions across the A1 neck. It does not prove Goldberg, exclude strict components at positive deficit, or handle cusp, collapse, multilevel, and diameter-divergent degenerations. Problems 1–3 remain live; in particular, the same matched Einstein analysis informs Q1 desingularization, while the certified sub-tariff cells and smooth-attainment questions remain unaffected.

mathematical_discussion:
This Step began by rewriting the coupled Kähler–Einstein/A1 problem in an exact nonlinear form. Earlier steps treated it as a linearized pair system. Now: an Einstein metric g is almost-Kähler Einstein (AKE) with self-dual ω exactly when the finite-dimensional space H⁺_g of closed self-dual forms contains an element of constant length √2. The overdetermined part of Goldberg is therefore a length map on a b⁺-dimensional sphere attached to each Einstein metric. In the earlier linearization this showed up as an infinite-dimensional cokernel; here it becomes a concrete finite object, the length defect λ(g).

At a negative KE metric or orbifold the length map is exactly rigid. H⁺ splits as Rω ⊕ Re H^{2,0}, the two summands are pointwise orthogonal, and so |aω+β|² = 2a²+|β|². A holomorphic 2-form of constant norm would trivialize K, which E<0 forbids. This gives the quadratic center estimate ‖Q₀(β)‖ ≥ c_V‖β‖² with Q₀(β)=|β|²−mean. It needs no H^{2,0}=0. It fails at E=0 (hyperkähler K3, flat tori), so negative curvature is the operative input.

The main construction answers Spirit's mixed-term question.
- Pure metric terms vanish through second order by Nagy's identity h₂⁺=h₁², which keeps the fixed ω compatible.
- The mixed h–β source in the self-duality equation is genuinely nonzero, but it is exactly the first-order Griffiths-transversal transport of the holomorphic 2-form along the Kodaira–Spencer direction. This transport exists for every ∂̄-closed direction by the ∂∂̄-lemma, with no integrability or unobstructedness needed. It keeps the transported form pointwise orthogonal to ω.
- Therefore the complete second-order obstruction, modulo all admissible corrections and simultaneous gauge, is Q₀(β₁). The tangent form-rotation center is quadratically killed, uniformly in the metric direction.

The structural lesson is that a non-Kähler entrance cannot come from rotating ω inside H⁺; it must come from Einstein metrics that are themselves not Kähler. The form sector is slaved to the metric sector.

At the singular scale the decisive new input is the indicial structure of closed self-dual forms on flat cones. Homogeneous solutions exist only in degrees d≥0 and d≤−4. Inversion composed with a reflection maps d to −d−4, which proves this in all degrees. Degree 1 is killed for nontrivial Γ⊂SU(2), and on the A1 cone the constant mode is isolated in the gap (−4,2) with no logarithms. With the exact flux law F_i(r)=∫α∧r^{−4}ι_Xω_i, the constant trace across a moving neck drifts only by the integrated metric error, which is ρ_n²+R_n^{−4}→0 for the naive model. Hence slow logarithmic rotation, invisible to the L⁴ torsion energy, is forbidden by closedness and self-duality alone.

Consequences of the neck-trace theorem:
- The bubble's parallel form equals ω_V(p).
- Harmonic self-dual forms are uniformly bounded and converge across orientation-matched Kähler ALE degenerations, including multiple sites and any Γ.
- b⁺(M)=b⁺(V).
- The quadratic center constant is lower-semicontinuous as the core scale tends to 0.
- Together with the first desingularization obstruction (R⁺(p)=(s/4)I⊗I, kernel I^⊥), the AK form sees Eguchi–Hanson as the smoothing: the vanishing sphere is asymptotically Lagrangian.

The orbifold charge identity T₊(M)=T₊(V) gives D(g)=(Ŝ²(g)−Ŝ²(V))/16. So a strict AKE metric near a KE orbifold is exactly an AKE Einstein metric with positive normalized-action excess.

With form centers, core traces and transverse EH data removed, the endpoint problem at a smoothable A1 point reduces to the normal derivative ∂_{ζ_I}Λ_I=A+o(1) of one raw obstruction function in one real variable, with A=c₀s/4≠0. This C¹ (not C⁰) uniformity is precisely the missing uniform inverse. Ozuch's estimates control values, not ζ-derivatives. The Kähler-smoothing graph in period coordinates (q~ζ₂+iζ₃, c~q²) also requires a genuine local-to-global smoothing map.

The complementary monopole test was useful mainly as a negative result. The Step-88 fork asked whether the topology of the O10 endpoint can be seen by a line section whose derivative is controlled without W⁻. That means a section built only from Φ and ∇Φ, whose bounds come from (A.12), because the curvature of S⁺ contains no W⁻. Representation theory alone does not answer this. Equivariant polynomials of nonzero charge exist in abstract.

The decisive fact is geometric: the endpoint first jet has a stabilizer.
- Taking ζ=0 together with DΦ=0 forces ∇Φ=e₂⊗s⁻⊗e₂. The derivative points away from Φ, and its covector half has rank one in S⁻.
- So the endpoint first jet is one Spin^c orbit of dimension 6.
- It is fixed by a circle that combines a rotation of the tangent space with a gauge transformation. That circle rotates the fibre of L with weight 2.
- Every natural first-order charged section therefore vanishes at the endpoint. This is a rigidity of the endpoint jet itself, not a failure of the search.

At second order the circle breaks, but not completely.
- The surviving finite-density coefficient c is exactly the unique charge-5 weight vector. The script reproduces |σ|²=4ρ*m*³ with ratio 1.
- So a ℤ₅ subgroup still fixes the second-order data, and L⁵ is the minimal visible line.
- The O10 proof's choice of σ is forced.
- Any such section has derivative of order ∇³Φ. By the Step-47 per-core integrals, that derivative scales with the density of W⁻.

Complementarily, the torsion τ ∈ S⁻⊗L is first order in Φ. It has density-free H¹ bounds and nearly constant length. Its bundle has c₂=(9a²+T₋)/4, which is 5χ+6τ in the Kähler case. But the curvature of that rank-two bundle sees W⁻. Dense Taub–NUT nuts are zeros of τ with H¹-cheap, critical-scale energy, and their charge is carried by W⁻.

The density-free problem is thus exactly the mismatch between two bundles:
- the W⁻-free line bundles have no natural density-free section;
- the rank-two bundle has such a section, but it sees W⁻.
Any theorem must break this mismatch by a nonlocal argument, or by critical H¹ control of the Nijenhuis phase c. A counterexample would have to realize a closed c-depleted nut phase.

The same U(2) algebra shows that almost-Kähler pairs have no natural first-order K^m sections. Canonical-line information in Goldberg arguments must therefore come from curvature (η) or from second jets. This explains structurally why Steps 77–82 kept landing on η and dd^c log q, and it advises against more first-order torsion bookkeeping.

Spirit #118 sets the scope. Finite-density O10 already covers k/A<1/3, so this result clarifies the χ/A→∞ regime and the tools for Q4, not Q1. Q1's real issue remains the same-metric alignment deficit, or a direct incompatibility with exact Einstein metrics.

A02's Wahl orbifold V turns α(X#4CP̄²)=0 into the question of whether some non-Kähler negative Einstein orbifold exists on V. Local isotropy at the cone points gives constraints invisible to H² and K²:
- forced monopole zeros for twists j≥2;
- ∇Φ(p)=0;
- J(p)=±J₀ for any almost-Kähler form;
- torsion zeros of order at least 2.
None of these is yet an obstruction, because the index count is positive. They are the right local inputs to combine with the deformation theory of the cone, or with the identification of which twist coset supplies the Seiberg–Witten class.

These results are not yet independently checked. The TTCS verifier s89_t11_tool1 is pending.

mathematical_discussion:
Step 90 separated four mathematical layers that Step 89 had partially conflated: the algebra of the ideal monopole first jet, the finite-density endpoint of the bounded resolvent v, the local Taub–NUT model formed from the raw torsion τ, and the global determinant-line topology. The first-jet orbit result survives: the calibrated pair (Φ,∇Φ) is one Spin^c(4) orbit with a circle stabilizer acting nontrivially on every nonzero power of L, so a charged pointwise first-jet section vanishes on that orbit. This is a real structural obstruction to lowering the finite-density line construction to first order. It does not imply density-independent H¹ estimates for arbitrary first-jet formulas. The delayed independent verifier confirmed the orbit, stabilizer, Clifford normalization, and charge-five representation, while showing that the one-mode analytic theorem concerns ∇v rather than ∇τ, that the weight multiset is {-2,-1,1,1,2,2,4,5}, that the residual Z5 statement applies only to the specified augmented endpoint, and that a rank-two nearly unit H¹ section can retain nonzero c2 through an inexpensive point zero. These corrections were inserted into the Step-89 note.

The decisive new calculation tests the actual projection rather than inferring its behavior from the full tensor norm. In the parallel hyperkähler spinor frame on exact Taub–NUT, with Φ_TN=√ρ_* e1+a f̄ e2 and τ_TN=√(m_*/2)d f̄, the local analogue of the charge-five section is exactly
σ_TN=(2048√6/2187) ℓ f̄/(r+ℓ)^3.
A symbolic exterior-algebra/Clifford computation proves this identity with zero residual; floating evaluations at generic points independently agree. The mode is a dipole: it vanishes on the two-dimensional preimage f^{-1}(0), including sheets reaching the block boundary, and decays as ℓr^{-2}. Its ordinary Dirichlet energy is the scale-invariant 268435456π²/55801305, and its L² mass is (67108864π²/4782969)ℓ². The energy inside B_R and its exterior tail were integrated exactly, showing concentration at r comparable to ℓ rather than at the nut or in a long collar. More importantly, the gauge-invariant amplitude satisfies ∫|d|σ_TN||²=67108864π²/33480783=(5/12)∫|dσ_TN|², so Kato gives the same positive lower bound for every unitary connection on this fixed section. The connection cannot erase the amplitude cost, but this is not yet a universal payment for actual endpoint sequences.

The model is depleted rather than nearly constant: on a flux-radius block R_ℓ comparable to ℓ^(1/3), the normalized fraction where |σ_TN| exceeds any fixed positive threshold is O(ℓ^(1/2)). Under the inherited common-connection hypotheses v−τ→0 in normalized H¹, bounded v, and |τ|²→m_* in normalized L², truncation and Hölder imply Φ∧[t(v)−t(τ)]→0 in normalized L¹. Thus an H¹-close bounded resolvent preserves depletion in measure, although not derivative energy. This directly separates the dense nut phase from the positive-modulus resolvent endpoint used in the finite-density line theorem.

The determinant-line square also cannot simply be assigned to the nuts. From F_A=F_0+e with bounded F_0 and e→0 in normalized L², the normalized integral of F_A∧F_A over any normalized-volume-vanishing set tends to zero. A phase with V/ℓ² fixed-scale nuts occupies only O(ℓ²) normalized volume. Those cores may carry W− curvature and rank-two degree, but not the nonzero normalized Chern–Weil square of L^5. Any localization of the line class on the zero sheets requires a relative transgression and phase/boundary matching argument. Consequently, the next substantive problem is no longer another total covariant-energy coefficient; it is whether a finite marked multi-nut block can match the depleted phase, zero sheets, determinant connection, and exterior actual fields while retaining the required global line square, or whether that matching forces payment elsewhere.

The Wahl analysis was also repaired. The tested characters ζ^(nj) are precisely boundary twists extending over B_{n,1}; they do not enumerate the extra complement cosets. A general twist ζ^r has positive-spinor weights (r,r−n), and r=1 admits an invariant first derivative. Hence ∇Φ(p)=0 holds for the tested extendible family, not every orbifold Spin^c lift. Smooth filler transfer supplies scalar and mixed-curvature inequalities but no particular orbifold monopole. The almost-Kähler isotropy result remains independent: the invariant self-dual direction is ±ω_0 and the torsion has the recorded high-order zero, but this local fact currently yields no global contradiction.

For the full Einstein-gap programme, this Step does not alter the certified strict-saving smooth construction, the unresolved unrestricted optimum, smooth attainment, or closed Goldberg. It does sharpen the common realizability problem: topology can be carried locally by W− and rank-two degree while the determinant-line topology remains global and must pass through phase and relative boundary data. The Wahl orbifold remains a genuine Q1 existence alternative, but no supplied field yet links its local characters to an Einstein obstruction. The first-jet stabilizer remains useful for Q4 only as an explanation of why curvature, second jets, or global transport are unavoidable.

Further progress needs a genuinely new non-averaged estimate or a closed construction, not more block bookkeeping. An orbifold point is a flat-cone orbifold point, so in the uniformizing chart an orbifold Einstein metric is just a Γ-invariant smooth Einstein germ, and local cone counting imposes no constraint. mathematical_discussion:
The central difficulty across Q1–Q4 remains same-metric realizability: topology can be carried by W⁻ curvature, Ricci-flat fillers, or collapse without aggregate Ricci payment, while actual monopole, harmonic-form, phase, period, and boundary equations may still prevent the assembly. Step 92 corrected several apparent reductions before choosing a stronger entrance. The absence of Z² subgroups in a ball-quotient group does not remove cusps whose boundary map has a kernel, and non-virtual-nilpotence does not remove bounded-curvature collapse. Filler transfer selects no orbifold spinᶜ character, and an extending structure is not automatically supplied by Seiberg–Witten theory. The Taub–NUT calculation remains a consistency model for selected averages rather than an exhaustive description of dense-carrier phases.

Independent verification strengthened A02's cap result while narrowing its exact scope. Under hypotheses (E), the cap charge is a well-defined ordered iterated limit; fixed-link C² convergence controls the APS eta term, nested shells give monotonicity, and total tail-volume convergence makes cap scalar energy vanish. If one cap meets several ends, the theorem directly gives the limiting sum of their link charges unless separate end asymptotics are supplied. The transferred mixed estimate is genuinely 9k+8Σc_j≤3A. Extra charge-four ball caps change the Hopf formula to k+32N+32B≤3A. A four-class Hopf cap has c₊=0 but c₋=20 and therefore concentrates 40π² of W⁻ energy; it is not curvature-energy-free. No immediate parity obstruction follows because −D₄ is an index-two even sublattice of −I₄, the characteristic square matches the signature modulo eight, and the relevant closed spinᶜ index is zero. The meaningful collapse experiment is consequently a marked D₄ ALF core, its actual complement, and the matching of their adiabatic end corrections—not a topology-only w₂ argument.

Four serious routes were compared. Ordinary entropy-degree comparison to a complex-hyperbolic host gives only u≥64A/81 after the Ricci entropy bound, weaker than the supplied monopole estimate u≥A; an Einstein-specific strain-rigidity theorem would be profound but was not found. The one-node quintic remains the strongest secondary closed-Goldberg route through the normalized CSCK residual and one fixed Ozuch reduction. The zero-charge Hopf cap is an exact local realization problem but still lacks an Einstein bulk. The main route is therefore fixed supplied-field transfer across the explicit Wahl recovery family, because it can place an identified actual field on a hypothetical non-Kähler Einstein orbifold and preserve information discarded by scalar–Weyl integrals.

The prescribed Ricci-flat filler geometry makes this transfer cheaper than first expected. Lemma 86.S gives uniformly bounded scalar curvature: the annular Ricci tensor is O(1), the filler is Ricci-flat, and the exterior is fixed. The monopole maximum principle therefore bounds |Φ_ε|² uniformly, while filled radius-R balls have volume O(R⁴). Hence spinor L⁴ mass and F_A⁺ energy cannot concentrate at a Wahl point. For a genuinely supplied finite signed family, a subsequence fixes one spinᶜ structure while retaining (a_ε⁺)²≥A. Global Weitzenböck and Chern–Weil identities then bound Φ in L⁴, ∇_AΦ in L², and full determinant curvature in L², and the surviving regular-part field has positive mass. The earlier complementary logarithmic-cutoff argument did not control the whole annular tail; it was corrected. A logarithmic outward cutoff remains useful only for a later scalar-L²-only generalization.

An explicit PPS character is also not a prerequisite. Relative to a fixed local lift, H²(BZ_{n²};Z)→H²(L(n²,n−1);Z) is an isomorphism, so the fixed marked complement structure determines a unique abstract orbifold lift res(s). For even n, the full spinᶜ lift must be retained because determinant doubling loses information. After finite-energy equivariant removal, rational-ball/cone replacement preserves the real determinant square. Lossless F_A⁺ transfer and Chern–Weil then force lossless full abelian curvature transfer; the integrated Weitzenböck identity likewise transfers spinor-gradient energy. Thus no hidden ASD abelian energy can remain in the shrinking filler or neck, even though metric W⁻ may concentrate. This sharpens the common realizability question: any new Einstein obstruction must come from differential compatibility, relative phase or lift data, or an index/transport relation—not from an unidentified gauge-energy bubble. The Hodge-defect and self-dual Weitzenböck formulas are valid enabling identities, but they do not yet provide that new relation.

mathematical_discussion:
Step 92 had selected the fixed-supplied-field limit (WFL) across a Wahl filler as the main route. The aim was to get an actual Seiberg–Witten field onto a hypothetical non-Kähler Einstein Wahl orbifold V, so that information lost by scalar–Weyl integrals could be used. This step turned that route into a theorem and found its exact limit.

The analytic part is now settled. In the abelian case, a point can be removed using only a bounded spinor and finite L² curvature: a point has zero W^{1,2} capacity in dimension 4, the Coulomb primitive on the ball is unique, and the system bootstraps to smoothness. Uniqueness of that primitive makes it Γ-invariant, and the residual phase cocycle Γ→R vanishes, so the extended lift is exactly res(s). With the bounded scalar curvature of the Lemma 86.S family, there is no loss of spinor mass, abelian curvature energy, or gradient energy in the filler or neck, and the real class square is preserved. Supply on V is therefore an actual theorem for every orbifold metric, given metric-wise supply on M.

An index-transfer lemma also holds. Both APS pieces vanish: the Ricci-flat Şuvaina filler has a flat determinant, and the cone can be replaced by a Γ-invariant psc cap. Kawasaki's local term singles out precisely the extendible characters nZ/n². This was checked numerically for n≤8, and the verifier supplied an exact proof for all n.

The structural finding is that the PPS Wahl orbifolds can be realized, by a marked existential choice, as complex orbifolds Y = X̂/[n+2,2,...,2]. Y is of general type and K_Y is not nef: the discrepancies are a_i=-(n-i)/n, so a (−1)-curve C meeting component i has K·C=-i/n<0. The Wahl branch of the Q1 trichotomy is therefore the orbifold analogue of Q1 on a non-minimal general-type orbifold, not a new mechanism. Its +-chirality package matches M exactly: a², T_+, Dirac index, supply, and the scalar/W⁺ LeBrun bounds. WFL thus reproduces LeBrun's k≥A/3 obstruction on V and nothing stronger. I first asserted a broader transfer principle; the verifier corrected it. T_-^orb, local characters, forced zeros and full SW invariants do not transfer, so 'Wahl = Q1' is an analogy, not an equivalence.

The genuinely new local data are these. For odd n≥3, the twist formula gives forced double zeros Φ(p)=∇Φ(p)=0 for 6/16 (n=3) or 8/16 (n≥5) of the sign classes on E1..E4. For n=2 no class has a forced zero. W⁺(p) has Kähler-type algebra diag(2,−1,−1) with free eigenvalue. The verifier added that the forced subfamily is closed under complementation, so averaging still gives (a⁺)²≥A over it. Hence a field with a forced double zero can be selected without losing the A bound, and ∫(s⁻)²>32π²A strictly on every orbifold metric. Class selection is therefore not the bottleneck.

The missing implication is now one sharp quantity: the dimensionless regularity scale λr_0² at the Wahl point. A lower bound on it would give a uniform defect c'λ²r_0⁴/n². If it can collapse, a marked forced character might migrate into shrinking Ricci-flat bubbles at vanishing defect. A bubble tree that retains the spinᶜ character is the natural tool. The alternative is a construction: a Kähler-wall degeneration on Y in which the forced zero divisor shrinks, which first requires identifying that divisor explicitly.

My strategic judgment is that the Wahl branch does not offer a cheaper road to Q1. Progress on Q1 needs either this marked-character bubble analysis or a genuinely Einstein-differential mechanism, and the same mechanism would bear on both branches. Q2–Q4 are unchanged by this step.

mathematical_discussion:
Step 94 asked whether Step 93's new capability—an actual supplied Seiberg–Witten field, with marked lift and energy preserved on a Wahl orbifold—can affect Einstein existence rather than merely strengthen scalar strictness. Spirit #125 identified the key logical gap: a forced spinor zero raises scalar undersaturation, but an Einstein candidate in the small-blowup range already has room for scalar excess inside the known scalar–W⁺ budget. The zero matters for Q1 only if it controls a combined same-structure quantity that cannot coexist with Ric°=0.

The Einstein feasible region was therefore reconstructed before committing to a marked bubble tree. For Ric=−(λ/4)g, S=λ²V, W=∫|W⁺|² and T₊^{orb}=A−k, Chern–Weil gives 4π²(A−k)=S/24+2W. The full one-field LeBrun estimate gives the corrected edge [√(8x)+√(A−k−x)]²≥6A, x=S/(96π²), hence x≥A[4−√(1−3k/A)]²/27 and D_W≥4π²k+(8π²A/9)[1−√(1−3k/A)]². This confirms Spirit's point: a local lower bound for λr₀² can be absorbed by moving upward from this edge and is not itself incompatible with Einstein geometry.

The weighted-pencil theory identifies the more consequential quantity. For the transferred class, a²=T₊^{orb}=A−k. The exact deficits D_β decompose into the signed monopole slack, a nonnegative sign term and β⁻¹∫(s+β√6|W⁺|)². At an exact Einstein metric the corpus gives positive non-saturation for every β>2, but this supplies additional lower half-planes in the global curvature variables rather than an exclusion throughout 0<k<A/3. The only degenerate endpoint is β=2, where negative Kähler–Einstein geometry is genuinely realized. There the theory retains an actual weighted monopole for the same Spin^c structure, its harmonic projection, a bounded polynomial self-dual form and a polynomial Weyl model. Small D₂ forces amplitude, harmonic alignment, derivative energy and W⁺ alignment toward the Kähler model. A forced zero excludes exact saturation for each fixed metric, but a zero neighborhood can shrink in four dimensions. Thus the marked field must quantitatively enter D₂, or an equivalent retained alignment sum, rather than scalar slack alone. Even such a payment must then be combined with projection control and a topological upper relation before it can contradict P=0.

The marked lens-space data were examined for a scale-independent transport quantity. The useful TTCS analysis found that every extendible twist has the same relative Dirac eta term as the canonical lift; the extendible subgroup is isotropic for the lens-space linking form; any isolated normalized-spinor degree has no character-forced fractional residue; ordinary Chern–Simons, stress, Weitzenböck and Pohozaev fluxes vanish on shrinking links; and W⁺(p)=μ diag(2,−1,−1) has no scale-independent local mass. Flat marked holonomy is genuine information, but the Ricci-flat Wahl filler carries it at zero abelian curvature cost. The first unexploited local datum is therefore the leading equivariant monogenic Taylor mode and its curvature-sensitive continuation, not another APS or Chern–Weil number.

An exact polynomial-mode computation was then created. The first implementation paired the Step-93 fibre weights with a non-intertwining Dirac matrix and falsely reported first degree ℓ=n. Focused independent verification exposed the mismatch. The script was corrected to the equivariant flat operator D⁺=[[∂z₁,∂bar z₂],[−∂z₂,∂bar z₁]], and the data were regenerated exactly over the rationals. The corrected result is ℓ_min(n,j)=2 min(j−1,n−j) for every forced extendible twist j=2,…,n−1. For the actual forced sign classes supplied by Proposition 93.C when odd n≥5, the twists occur at j=(n−1)/2,(n+1)/2,(n+3)/2 with multiplicities 1,6,1, so every such supplied field vanishes to order at least n−3, while the middle six can first occur at order n−1; n=3 gives order at least two. This is much stronger local Taylor information than Step 93's order-two statement, but it still accelerates the decay of unscaled link fluxes rather than producing a residue or a uniform D₂ payment.

The scientific decision is consequently sharper than either abandoning Wahl or immediately building a marked bubble tree. First determine whether the coupled Einstein–Seiberg–Witten Taylor recursion turns the high-order marked mode into a signed D₂ or Weyl-alignment contribution. The flat Dirac map is surjective on polynomial target sectors, so the first metric-curvature source may be freely absorbed by a higher spinor coefficient; the curvature equation and Bianchi compatibility must be retained before any obstruction is inferred. If the coupled recursion also has full local freedom, further bubble-tree classification would transport no quantity capable of resolving Q1, and effort should return to Q4 or Q2/Q3. If a signed same-structure term survives, it gives exactly the datum a marked bubble tree should transport.
